213th-fleet.title: 213th Fleet
213th-fleet.content:

Imperial naval fleet. Headquartered at Efate, with a forward operating base in the Pixie system.

40th-squadron.title: 40th Squadron
40th-squadron.content:
traveller sota faction
Secrets of the Ancients
One of the best-organised Vargr bands in Gvurrdon.

Descended from a squadron of Vargr warships that survived the First Frontier War and established their own petty kingdom in the chaotic aftermath
Controls a loose alliance of about half a dozen systems
Individual planets have their own governments, but the 40th’s naval officers are the real power in the empire
Lacks the resources to maintain its full fleet without external help — in the past the Zhodani have propped them up to threaten the Imperium’s flank

A Vargr power bloc that answers to naval officers and has taken foreign money to menace the Imperium before.

aail.title: Aail
aail.content:
traveller sota npc alell
Secrets of the Ancients
Representative of the Brotherhood of Humaniti, who arrived at Vlen’s homecoming in Vaca Goya in Session 2026-10-18. Name heard as “Ail”/“Ayl”; spelled Aail in the filename of the GM’s image.

Came in dancing, in green robes (hers very revealing), shaved head, three monks behind her chanting a mantra while she spoke.
Her claim

The initiate Zu, known to the secular world as Vlen Backett, was a member of our order some years ago. He fled our monastery in the dead of night and never returned. As part of his initiation he signed over all worldly goods to the Brotherhood of Humaniti. It has taken us some time to find Zu’s homeworld, and now we are here. We claim what is rightfully ours.

(Transcribed as “Zoo”; Rich spells it Zu.)
The monks have paperwork for the signing-over. According to Porter Sajan, they also want their own ceremony for their initiate, “some DNA thing that will take hours”. See Claims on Vlen’s Estate.
Manner
Hugs everyone, warmly and at length (“Blessed be the child”, “we must protect you, sweet child”). Hans Backett was mortified. StClair hugged her and was left euphoric. He then realised he may have passed her contact contamination from the plants he’d picked, and said nothing.
Notes

alahir.title: Alahir
alahir.content:
traveller sota ship
Secrets of the Ancients
A ship that reportedly arrived at Regina Highport several weeks before the party’s investigation.
It is registered to the Scout Service but is not a standard scout design. The ship and all other information about it came through Admiral Cassius’s network and have not been independently verified.
Connections

Its unnamed captain reportedly held numerous meetings with Pallod Norrim
Offworlders have reportedly been seen operating in POC uniforms since the Alahir arrived
The local POC are rumoured to be angry that an Imperial police force has taken over a murder inquiry
A further rumour claims the murdered person was a Zhodani spy and the inquiry is now a state-security matter; the victim’s identity and the claim itself remain unconfirmed

Odoy’s account — 195-1105
Detective Odoy told the crew that the Imperial force which arrived aboard the Alahir is hunting Ven Yasha, and that the Zhodani-spy rumour is a fabrication — the murder it refers to is Vlen Backett’s, and the spy framing exists to justify the Imperial takeover of the inquiry. He also says that force took both Dancado attackers, removing the surviving prisoner from POC custody.
Unverified, but it is consistent with the reported offworlders in POC uniforms and with Pallod Norrim having gone unreachable.
Open questions

What kind of ship it actually is
Who commands and crews it
Why its captain has been meeting Pallod
Whether its personnel were involved at Dancado or used the grav car seen leaving the scene

Departed â€” 196-1105
Exceedingly Discreet told the crew that Imperial Intelligence were on Regina in numbers, that they arrived aboard the Alahir, and that the ship has since departed â€” whatever their business was, it is concluded.

The captain’s name was heard at the table as “Gand Hulses” â€” spelling unconfirmed, check with the GM â€” and he is said to hold some special portfolio within the intelligence services
Exceedingly Discreet does not know whether they came for Ven Yasha or for something else, which leaves Detective Odoy’s claim unconfirmed rather than contradicted

If the ship is gone, the crew’s plan to investigate it on Regina is dead, and the departure itself is a data point: the Imperial interest in this case may have finished before the crew got near it.

alell-starport.title: Alell Starport
alell-starport.content:
traveller sota location alell
Secrets of the Ancients
The Class B surface starport of Alell. Alell has no port in orbit, so this is the only place to land. A pinnace like the Implacable can use it; the Event Horizon can’t.

What’s known

Its original structure dates back to the First Imperium, and is considered an excellent example of fin-de-siècle Vilani design
Refined fuel, maintenance and spacecraft construction facilities (Starport B, from the UWP)
The Jocell Family are descended from a Backett cousin who left Vaca Goya for work at the starport

From Tel’s picture and map

The main building is a huge stepped pyramid of grey stone or concrete, with a tall entrance arch on one face. Small craft are parked on its flat top, and another flies overhead
A tall round tower stands beside it, and there’s a second tower further off
The pyramid sits on a cleared square in red, orange and purple jungle, with mountains behind and a river running past
A road leads from the pyramid to a round gatehouse set in the wall of a walled town with a street grid. A second round structure stands near the river, and there’s a small cluster of buildings beside the pyramid

Inferences, not stated: the round structures on the map are probably the towers in the picture. The walled town fits the history’s description of the old lodges, which are now walled cities. Neither is confirmed, and the town isn’t named.
Notes


Session 2026-10-18: the Implacable flew straight into the mouth of the pyramid: a gigantic artificial cavern, more temple than landing site, big enough to swallow a warship, with plenty of room. Arriving craft are sprayed with chemical disinfectant under strong UV light, as biological control

Customs: everything is scanned and disinfected. Nothing may be imported; guns stay aboard. Vlen’s cryotube went through too, and the scanner glitched on it: screens glitched, confused faces. It passed on a second run and was put down to a system glitch
Air-shuttle taxis and their pilots wait outside. Rao works from here
There’s a cargo handling station in orbit, but nothing that can help the Event Horizon

alell.title: Alell
alell.content:
traveller sota location
Secrets of the Ancients
World in the Regina subsector of the Spinward Marches.
Homeworld of Vlen Backett, who returned for a few weeks or a month or two at a time between voyages. The wider Backett family appears to be based here — and Vlen’s remains are to be brought back here for burial.
See the Alell Family Tree for the whole family and everyone else at the homecoming, on one page.
The world
Originally settled by the descendants of hotel staff, Alell has become a rich and influential world despite its extremely dangerous native wildlife. The population clusters into a small number of fortified cities, though modern technology makes rural living possible.

Primary industry: tourism
Secondary exports: wood, furs, pharmaceuticals and other material harvested from the jungles covering 30% of the surface
Class B starport, its original structure dating back to the First Imperium and considered an excellent example of fin-de-siècle Vilani design

A rich tourist world with lethal jungles and a pharmaceutical trade — and the man who grew up here died full of a plant-derived narcotic.
The system — as found, c. 219-1105

No gas giant and no highport. No way to refuel by skimming
A lot of radiation from the system’s sun, enough to interfere with sensor scans
In orbit, a cargo handling station, a medical facility, and a rapid-response emergency service for rescuing people lost in the jungle. None of them take visiting ships
A surface starport (Alell Starport) that a pinnace like the Implacable can use and a lab ship can’t
Doesn’t normally have patrol ships assigned, per Ozy’s Computers check. Delta 2 claims to be one anyway
The GM’s framing: “a bit of an arse-end”, a toxic, poisonous jungle world used for hunting in the past, with very old First Imperium buildings. More to come when he reads out the world text
From the chapter’s arrival text (Session 2026-10-04, paraphrased): Alell circles an angry, energetic star, so ships shelter in the planet’s shadow to spare their hulls. From orbit the jungles show gold and red, with the lights of walled resorts scattered here and there. Getting here from Regina along the Spinward Main means a string of systems with no starport worth the name, refuelling from gas giants or automated hydrogen harvesters
No starport in space at all, only on the surface. The Event Horizon can’t dock anywhere, and Hull repairs can’t be had here

Universal World Profile — from Tel’s pre-session handout
Imperium B46789C-A · Regina subsector · Hex 1706 · Rich (Ri)


















































StarportBGood starport: refined fuel, maintenance and spacecraft constructionSize46,400 km diameter, about 0.45gAtmosphere6Standard, breathableHydrographics7About 70% surface waterPopulation8Hundreds of millions — 203 million in a published 1100 censusGovernment9Impersonal BureaucracyLaw LevelC (12)Extremely restrictiveTechnologyA (TL10)Early stellar
Law Level 12 is higher than Regina’s 9.
History — from Checking In Indefinitely: A History of Alell (Tharsis Djar, Alell Free Press, 1101)

On Alell, ferocity and beauty go together. The jungles shimmer red and gold, but touch the wrong frond with bare skin and a poison stinger lashes out. The Whisperhawk stoops on its prey from the green clouds. Even the sky is dangerous: the auroras are bursts of radiation from the primary star
Settled in the dying days of the First Imperium. Hunting the whisperhawk, the malificent and the “vicious glittering” Lambdragon became fashionable among nobles, who built hunting lodges in the most scenic spots: atop the glacial cliffs, in the heart of the Dranxi Jungle, and on the savannah hunting grounds of the cadegeree. Each lodge had a staff of technicians, groundskeepers and servants
Then the First Imperium collapsed. When explorers from the resurgent Imperium re-contacted Alell several hundred years later, the descendants of those hotel porters and safari guides had built a civilisation around the lodges. The lodges are now walled cities, keeping out the jungle
Vaca Goya, the Backetts’ home, has a village porter as one of its leading dignitaries — presumably a title that comes down from the lodge staff (inference)

The book calls the lambdragon “vicious”; the creature handout calls it a gentle herbivore that can still be dangerous. Kept both.
Culture
The hotel-staff origin still runs through the language:

Hos — an inferior or servant, from the old Vilani dialect term hos’ai, servant or staff in the catering industry
Siu — a term of respect, from the old Vilani Siu’ch, meaning guest or honoured visitor

A world that divides everyone into staff and guests, and got rich on it.
Wildlife

Lambdragon — huge herbivore; a stampede can flatten a tank
Maleficent — jet-black tentacled predator, possibly not native to Alell
Whisperhawk — common canopy avian, stupid and prone to smothering things
Cadgeree — winged snake that drops on prey from height; confirmed as an Alell species by Tel’s “Monsters of Alell” handout, hunted on the savannah

People — from Tel’s pre-session handout, as Kostas knows them
Ahead of the next session, Tel gave Kostas’s background on the people likely to be at Vlen’s burial. Nearly all of it is what Kostas’s parents told him, so it’s second-hand.

Backett Family — Vlen’s closest living kin on Alell, from Vaca Goya: Tomas Backett, Hans Backett, Gunter Backett, Nairal Backett
Jocell Family — the Backett branch that moved to the starport: Marisa Jocell and her son Bard Jocell
Porter Sajan — Vaca Goya’s village porter, one of its most important dignitaries
Parad Family — unrelated local criminal gang under Yusul Parad, who may have lent Vlen money

Notes

The Event Horizon is bound here, departed Regina 196-1105, three jumps via Forboldn. Five high passengers paying Cr60,000 each on arrival. Vlen’s body was not brought along — corrected: Vlen’s body was transferred to the ship and came with them
Ozy’s homeworld Uakye is next door

Session 2026-09-27: arrived, c. 219-1105, and went straight into a fight with Delta 2 before reaching orbit. One jump of fuel left in the tanks. Passage fees not yet collected
Session 2026-10-04: Delta 2 destroyed in-system. The Event Horizon is parked in orbit in the planet’s shadow, badly damaged, and the Implacable took the passengers down: Cr300,000 collected. The local authorities can be told what happened but can’t do much from orbit. Chapter 2 starts here: less investigation, lots of NPCs, and some of them are Kostas’s family. The GM says Alell is where Kostas was born
Session 2026-10-18: down on the surface. What the table learned:

Customs and law: blades allowed, because people need them in the jungle. Armour and vacc suits fine; guns banned, so firearms stay aboard ship. Absolutely nothing imported. Taking anything off-world is “somewhat frowned upon”: “everything here is pretty much trying to kill you”
The plant life gives off a toxic gas that affects anyone not acclimatised, so visitors wear protective suits unless in vacc suits. Visitors get free misters, hand sprayers of fauna and flora repellent. The mist damages skin, another reason for the suits. Shuttles carry misters too
Most settlements have high walls; smaller ones use a sensor grid of mist-sprayer poles instead, as at Vaca Goya. Go into the jungle in a group, with a guide
Since its rediscovery after the First Imperium, Alell has become a mix of science and conservation (per Rao). Hunting lodges aren’t allowed now (per Nairal Backett)
Main trade: exotic furs and unusual minerals and ores (per Tomas Backett)
Trees taller than skyscrapers; flocks of whisperhawks; the aurora casts blood-red shadows. “Very reminiscent of the Jurassic”
Air shuttles with pilots work like taxis from the starport. It’s dangerous to fly out late in the day

ancients-extinction-theories.title: Ancients Extinction Theories
ancients-extinction-theories.content:
traveller sota clue
Secrets of the Ancients
The Ancients vanished abruptly some 300,000 years ago. The sudden extinction is a mystery to archaeologists, who have produced several competing theories. Mainstream thinking divides along two axes.
Homogenous vs Heterogenous

Homogenous — there was a single Ancients culture that expanded and then vanished. Explains the similarities between sites: commonalities in architecture, the use of Droyne as pets or servants, and so on.
Heterogenous — there were multiple competing cultures, a series of empires, or even multiple races that reached high technology in the Ancients period. Explains the wild variation in Ancients technology and architecture, the lack of clear structure to their territory, and the sudden end of their civilisation.

Catastrophist vs Gradual Decline

Catastrophist — a single terrible event ended the Ancients hegemony. Homogenous Catastrophists point to disease, a hostile alien race, or a strange accident. Heterogenous Catastrophists suggest civil war.
Gradual Declinist — a super-civilisation would be more robust than that; the Ancients must have slowly declined in vitality and viability over millennia.

Why it’s in the file
Most Ancients sites show damage consistent with orbital bombardment, and some systems show anomalies explicable only by weapons that destroyed whole planets. Whatever happened, it was violent, and Ujinka’s Research was a method for finding what’s left of it.
Notes

assiniboia.title: Assiniboia
assiniboia.content:
traveller sota location
Secrets of the Ancients
The gas giant that Regina orbits — Regina being technically a moon, not a planet. Assiniboia in turn orbits the locus of the primary star Lusor and its companion Speck; a third star, a red dwarf, runs a long eccentric orbit.
Lagrangian points: one of five positions in a three-body orbital configuration where a small object affected only by gravity stays stationary relative to the two larger bodies. With Assiniboia’s multiple moons, the system has several semi-stable points — the natural places to park something you don’t want found.
Notes

assumption-of-custody.title: Assumption of Custody
assumption-of-custody.content:
traveller sota law
Secrets of the Ancients
Under Regina law, the Regina Public Order Commission has the power to detain suspects for up to a month without trial.
Assumption of Custody is a process where multiple suspects of a crime are detained and questioned. These “suspects” might just have been in the area of the crime, or match a profile, or even be randomly swept off the streets.

Those Assumed into custody are innocent until proven guilty
Assumption is held to be a civic service, and a small stipend is available to those Assumed
It can still cause considerable inconvenience

Critics of the policy note that most citizens of Regina are never Assumed, while certain groups are detained regularly: known criminals, transients, uneducated youths — and Travellers.


                  
                  This aims directly at the party 
                  
                

They are Travellers, newly arrived on 193-1105, present at a double murder at Dancado, already tailed by a Commission grav car, and Kostas Backett is the surviving next of kin in a killing the Commission described to him only as “irregularities”.
A month’s detention without trial would end the investigation and let the third man walk. It would also put the only four people who know what Ujinka’s Research was about in Commission cells, at the Commission’s convenience, entirely lawfully.


Notes

atora.title: Atora
atora.content:
traveller sota location
Secrets of the Ancients
City on Regina, the other half of the pair with Credo City. Startown lies between them and is technically divided between the two — each blames the other for the state of it.
Startown is a thin strip separating Atora from Credo.
One of the “more traditional cities” that resents Credo’s cosmopolitanism and its Core-world affectations.

atticus-brown.title: Atticus Brown
atticus-brown.content:
traveller sota npc
Secrets of the Ancients
Second gunner aboard the Event Horizon, alongside Gunner Gunnerson. Cheap — “they wanted to get off planet”. Nothing else known. Name as heard at the table, 196-1105.

Session 2026-09-27: “the Greenhorn”, Gunner 2. Put on the missile turret against Delta 2, since none of the player characters’ skills help with missiles, and launched three on turn 1
Session 2026-10-04: kept on the missile rack and fired all twelve, three a round in rounds 1, 2, 3 and 5. The salvos destroyed Delta 2. aylin-boro.title: Aylin Boro
aylin-boro.content:
traveller sota npc contact
Secrets of the Ancients
Contact. Retired admiral. Hates Tyrus Cassius.
Kostas Backett served under her right before he left the navy, so she remembers his face — but she has him confused with another idiot who was the son of her superior, so she has to be nice to him. She has no idea he’s a loser dropout.

backett-family.title: Backett Family
backett-family.content:
traveller sota faction alell
Secrets of the Ancients
The family of Vlen Backett and Kostas Backett, based in Vaca Goya on Alell. Vlen’s closest living kin still on the planet.

Heads of the family: Tomas Backett, a local merchant, and his cousin brother (corrected at the table) Hans Backett, a hunter and trapper
Gunter Backett, 15, Tomas’s son
Nairal Backett, 92, Kostas’s great-uncle and the oldest member of the family
The Jocell Family are a branch of the Backetts, descended from a cousin who left Vaca Goya for the starport. They call the Backetts their “country bumpkin cousins”

Expected to gather for Vlen’s burial.
Source: Tel’s pre-session handout on Alell, mostly what Kostas’s parents have told him.
See the Alell Family Tree for the whole family and everyone else at the homecoming, on one page.
Notes


Session 2026-10-18: family tree corrected at the table. Tomas and Hans are brothers, not cousins, and Nairal is their uncle, which makes him Kostas’s great-uncle. Kostas reckons Tomas is his uncle

Kostas’s parents were at the homecoming. His mother Henna Backett fawned over the Admiral (“so good to see you again”). His father is Merrick Backett: “You look a mess, boy.”
Nobody was sad about Vlen. “We’re all waiting for that will reading”
No family security: “we’re not well-to-do”
Two newcomers claim a place in the family: Orisa Backett says she was Vlen’s wife, and calls Kostas her nephew. See Claims on Vlen’s Estate

bard-jocell.title: Bard Jocell
bard-jocell.content:
traveller sota npc alell
Secrets of the Ancients
Son of Marisa Jocell, Jocell Family. Kostas’s parents remember him spending his days fawning over off-world nobles and tourists.
Source: Tel’s pre-session handout on Alell, mostly what Kostas’s parents have told him.
Appearance

Session 2026-10-18: “Her asshole of a son”, nose as high as it goes. Impressed by the Admiral: “But Mother, his medals!” Marisa dragged him away

beck's-world.title: Beck's World
beck's-world.content:
traveller sota location
Secrets of the Ancients
A former pirate base. A volcanic wilderness with a minimal biosphere and few natural resources.
Where Iaros Ujinka was working on Ujinka’s Research — links between G-Band Transmissions and sites of Ancient technology. She had just returned from here when she wrote to Vlen Backett offering the meeting he never made.
Graxius StClair’s ex-wife, Juni, is still there — Ujinka’s notes say Juni and her team are investigating the g-band signals at the Ancients site here.
Worth noting
A volcanic rock with no biosphere, no resources and a pirate history is not somewhere a university historian goes for the archives. Whatever drew Ujinka there, it was in the ground or in the sky — and she came back from it ready to ask for funding and a ship.
Notes

being-followed.title: Being Followed
being-followed.content:
traveller sota clue
Secrets of the Ancients
Ozymandius Forthrast keeps getting the feeling the party is being followed — and he’s right. A Regina Public Order Commission grav car tailed them on the way to meet Iaros Ujinka at Dancado.
The same Commission that summoned Kostas Backett to Regina, told him nothing about how his uncle actually died, and insisted he report to them on arrival.
During the attack, a grav car remained outside. As Kostas and StClair entered the upstairs lounge to retrieve Iaros Ujinka, they saw it flying away. They think it bore POC colours, but the identification is unconfirmed. Its departure immediately after the attack makes its role more suspicious, but does not establish whether its occupants were involved, observing, or fleeing danger.
The officers who later arrived said they were the only POC personnel in the area and thought the crew had misidentified the vehicle. Admiral Cassius subsequently learned that offworlders have reportedly operated in POC uniforms since the Alahir arrived at Regina Highport. That could explain the apparent POC vehicle, but the connection is an inference rather than confirmed fact.
Open questions

Whether Pallod Norrim ordered it
Whether it’s protection, supervision, or a threat
Whether the departing vehicle was definitely the same POC grav car that followed them
Why it left immediately after the attack rather than intervening
Whether it belonged to personnel from the Alahir
Whether Detective Odoy is connected

Notes

black-horizon's-growth-serum.title: Black Horizon's Growth Serum
black-horizon's-growth-serum.content:
traveller sota item
Secrets of the Ancients
A growth formula held by Black Horizon aboard the Event Horizon. According to Khei (to Ozy, Advocate Effect +7, in bed), Black Horizon were carrying cryogenically frozen carthus embryos and this serum separately. “Somehow the two of them met”: the embryos grew instantly, broke containment and escaped into the maintenance shafts. That’s why the carthuses were juveniles and weaker than adults.

All the embryo samples have been destroyed, per Kay. The serum has been kept
Kay’s offer: keep the incident quiet and the serum might be made available to the crew, if it would be useful to them. Not answered yet

What else it does, what it was for, and how the two “met” by accident are all unexplained. It’s Kay’s account only.
Notes

black-horizon.title: Black Horizon
black-horizon.content:
traveller sota faction
Secrets of the Ancients
One of two research companies chartering lab space aboard the Event Horizon, the other being Helix. Their labs are off limits to passengers.
Won the dispute with Helix over a joint discovery made with Helix equipment and Black Horizon research in the first jump out of Regina — Ozy’s log analysis put the discovery with them, and their contract does the rest. See Helix.
Their charter terms (per Ozy’s read): secretive, encrypt everything; claim exclusive patent rights on any breakthrough, pay no royalties; and the crew may not inspect the cargo they bring aboard. Their rep aboard is Khei. They also have their own security detail, with stunners.
The specimens. That cargo clause is how live juvenile carthuses came aboard unseen. They broke containment in the third jump, Whanga → Alell, and escaped into the maintenance shafts — “three, maybe four, possibly more”; Black Horizon’s own count was vague. They want them back alive and will pay. A security officer of theirs went into the vents with the crew; one carthus stunned so far.
Hunt over, Session 2026-09-27. Seven carthuses: four killed, three stunned and taken into containment by a Black Horizon xenobiologist and officers. Their security guard Pedro was badly bitten. Per Khei, the carthuses were frozen embryos that grew instantly after an accidental contact with their growth serum. The embryos are destroyed, the serum kept, and Kay has offered it to the crew in return for silence — see Black Horizon’s Growth Serum. The “appreciation” promised for bringing them back alive hasn’t been mentioned since.
At Alell, when Delta 2 announced an inspection, Ozy warned them first. Kay appreciated it.
Nothing else known about what they research.

Full name, per the logo: Black Horizon Research Group.
Notes


Session 2026-10-04: per the GM, Black Horizon incinerated the three stunned carthuses as too dangerous. No live specimens remain. The serum offer and the “appreciation” are both still outstanding

boughene.title: Boughene
boughene.content:
traveller sota location
Secrets of the Ancients
A scout base is established here as part of continued surveying operations coreward and spinward of the Imperium.
There is little else in the system of interest to Travellers, and the scout base is not open to visitors.
The g-band footprint — from Ujinka’s Research
Officially nothing here. Ujinka’s notes say otherwise:

The 1102 survey logged a g-band drop-off around the Boughene precursor ruins, the same footprint found in the Regina sub-sector
Her own log (Entry 884-A) orbiting Boughene IV, a gas giant with a high metal-rich asteroid density: sensor packet degradation at 4.2 GHz and a 0.03-second clock-drift on the nav computers
A trader pulled a statue from the asteroid belt — Ujinka judged it a fragment of a larger anchor array. Vlen Backett borrowed it and it is now aboard the Event Horizon
“Could something else be hidden away in this system?” — and Vlen intended to scan it with Ujinka’s g-band sensor system, per his own disks

A closed scout base, a system described as uninteresting, and an Ancient anchor array in its asteroid belt.
Notes

brotherhood-of-humaniti.title: Brotherhood of Humaniti
brotherhood-of-humaniti.content:
traveller sota faction
Secrets of the Ancients
A quasi-religious group that arose following confirmation of the Solomani Hypothesis — that all Humaniti stems from a single source.

Believes all humans should come together as one species, united under a common government
Any government or institution that opposes such radical unity is an enemy of the species and must be destroyed
Since its inception it has moved towards mysticism, attributing increasingly unlikely supernatural powers to ‘true Humaniti’ — the ur-race destroyed when The Ancients divided Humaniti into different ‘tribes’

Why this is in the file
This is the second movement on record whose theology turns on Ancients inheritance. The Church of the Chosen Ones holds that the Vargr are the Ancients’ heirs; the Brotherhood holds that the Ancients broke humanity and that a lost true version of it had powers worth recovering.
Both would have an interest in Ujinka’s Research — a method of locating Ancients sites. The Brotherhood is the one of the two that has doctrine explicitly licensing the destruction of institutions that stand in its way, and a university department is an institution.
Nothing connects the Brotherhood to either killing. Noted as a candidate, not a conclusion.
Notes


Session 2026-10-18: they turned up at Vlen’s homecoming on Alell: Aail, dancing, with three chanting monks, green robes and shaved heads. Vlen was one of them: “the initiate Zu”, a member some years ago, who fled their monastery in the dead of night and never returned. On joining he signed over all worldly goods, and they have the paperwork. It took them “some time to find Zu’s homeworld”. They also want a “DNA” ceremony for their initiate, which Porter Sajan says will take hours

The GM’s reading: an esoteric group who believe all humanity must unite as one, and who love every human “in a distinctly uncomfortable way”: “treat every human like you want nothing more than to keep them safe forever, like a collection of butterflies”
This is the first direct link between Vlen and the Brotherhood. The note above said nothing connected them to either killing. That’s still true of the killings, but Vlen ran from them (the gap between “fled” and “killed” is not bridged by anything said at the table)
See Claims on Vlen’s Estate

cadgeree.title: Cadgeree
cadgeree.content:
traveller sota species
Secrets of the Ancients
An animal, not a sophont.
A winged snake with a spiked tail. Extremely effective predators: they attack by hurling themselves down on prey from a great height, embedding their tail spikes deep into the target’s flesh, then thrashing wildly and snapping the victim’s spine.
Cadgeree usually attack smaller creatures, but have been known to attack humans when hungry.
Native to Alell — listed in Tel’s “Monsters of Alell” handout. Checking In Indefinitely, the in-world history of Alell, puts their hunting grounds on the savannah, where First Imperium nobles built hunting lodges to hunt them. That book spells it “cadegeree”.
Notes

carthus.title: Carthus
carthus.content:
traveller sota species
Secrets of the Ancients
Tall, pale creature that dwells in deep desert caves. Four limbs and an extremely flexible spine — it dislocates its joints at will and worms through cracks and crevices. Hides in dark surroundings and hunts from them. Normally sucks the moisture out of fungus and moss; will take other prey when it’s available. Bites: one got through Protection 10 armour for 3 END.
Juvenile carthuses were among the specimens Black Horizon brought aboard the Event Horizon under a contract clause that stopped the crew inspecting their cargo. They escaped into the maintenance shafts during the jump from Whanga to Alell — “three, maybe four, possibly more”. Black Horizon want them back alive and will pay for it; stunners recommended. No armour of their own; a single rifle hit from Ozy nearly killed one, and Kostas put it down with a stun stick.
What they were (per Khei): cryogenically frozen embryos that came into contact with Black Horizon’s Growth Serum by accident and grew instantly, which is why they were juveniles and weaker than adults. The rest of the embryo samples have been destroyed.
Hunt over, Session 2026-09-27. Seven in all: four killed, three stunned and taken into Black Horizon’s containment. Two broke into the control room and tore into the ship’s systems. At full strength they bite hard: 16, 13, 10 and 19 were rolled against the crew. One put Kostas unconscious through armour 5, and another took a chunk out of Pedro’s shoulder.
“Acid for blood” was a joke at the table that got a “yeah” — not treated as fact.
Name as heard; spelling unconfirmed (GM’s stat block not seen).
Notes


Session 2026-10-04: the three stunned ones are dead too. Per the GM, Black Horizon incinerated them, judging them too dangerous. Kostas had wanted to stock the airlocks with carthuses against boarders

church-of-the-chosen-ones.title: Church of the Chosen Ones
church-of-the-chosen-ones.content:
traveller sota faction
Secrets of the Ancients
A Vargr religious sect who believe Vargr are the chosen heirs of The Ancients, and therefore the rightful rulers of the galaxy.
At its height some 200 years ago; today more of a fringe cult.
Why it’s in the file
A movement whose entire theology rests on Ancients inheritance is, on the face of it, exactly the kind of group with a stake in who gets to Ancients sites first — and Ujinka’s Research was about locating them. Nothing connects the Church to the killings. It’s noted because the pieces sit next to each other, not because anyone has drawn a line.
Notes

claims-on-vlen's-estate.content:

Everyone who turned up at Vlen Backett’s homecoming in Vaca Goya wanting something from him (Session 2026-10-18). Porter Sajan has asked Kostas and the crew to act as intermediaries and resolve the claims before the burial and will reading tomorrow. He didn’t wait for a yes.
See the Alell Family Tree for the whole family and everyone else at the homecoming, on one page.
The will

There isn’t one in hand. It wasn’t among the effects the crew collected on Regina. Kostas told Sajan he had it, then admitted he didn’t
Sajan had been told Vlen would have a copy with him. By whom isn’t known. “There must be another copy somewhere”
Tomas Backett also assumed the crew brought it. The whole village is “waiting for that will reading”
The table wondered whether the statuette hides one. It was scanned: nothing inside, not hollow

credo-city.title: Credo City
credo-city.content:
traveller sota location
Secrets of the Ancients
Capital city of Regina, population 87 million, on the eastern edge of the continent of Noncredo. Called Credo in the library entries; “Credo City” is how the Commission’s paperwork refers to it.
Where Vlen Backett was murdered.
The city
Credo prides itself on its cosmopolitanism — a high transient population including many visitors from the Core worlds. Fashion and culture here are heavily influenced by those visitors, which causes friction with the more traditional cities on Regina. It is sometimes called ‘little Capital’, a mocking reference to its mimicry of Imperial high culture.
Despite the cultural pretensions, Regina’s curious and strict legal system is fully in effect: laws must be voted on by the entire population, and the justice system is as bureaucratic as it is enthusiastic, without being efficient at either. See Regina Public Order Commission and Assumption of Custody.
A city with a large transient population, and a legal regime that sweeps transients — see how those two facts sit together.
His body was held in a cryogenic facility here, pending transfer to Kostas Backett for transport home to Alell. It has since been transferred to the Event Horizon and is with the crew at Alell. His outstanding affairs and belongings were here too.
He was staying at the Regina Down TAS Hostel here when he was killed. The dealer Darrian Jak works back alleys around the commercial district. The estate of Dancado lies just outside the city, and The Flotsam is a bar here.
Winter Shipping, the company behind the last number recovered from Vlen’s comms, operates here and in Star Town.
Notes

dancado.title: Dancado
dancado.content:
traveller sota location
Secrets of the Ancients
A forested region north of Credo City, on Regina — private property of the Duke of Regina. Home of Iaros Ujinka.


                  
                  Whose land this is 
                  
                

The Regina Public Order Commission acts “in the name of his grace the Duke”. A professor was shot dead on the Duke’s own private ground, with a Commission grav car parked outside; the party killed one intruder and subdued another there. Ujinka living on ducal land at all says something about her standing — or her patronage.


Iaros Ujinka was shot dead here, through a window, while meeting the party. They had been tailed to the estate by a Regina Public Order Commission grav car — see Being Followed.
The attack: power cut, security drone destroyed, Iaros Ujinka shot dead through the upstairs lounge window, front door broken down. Two men came upstairs; one was killed and the other knocked unconscious — the same two from the hostel footage. A third shooter stayed outside throughout and never entered.
The authorities took control of the scene and the surviving intruder entered POC custody. Before they arrived, he mentioned Ven Yasha during a brief questioning by the crew.
Aftermath

Kostas Backett and StClair got Ujinka to the autodoc, but it was too late to revive her
StClair treated Kostas, restoring 1 END and bringing him to END 1
Ozy recovered data concerning Ujinka’s Research, Vlen and the g-band work; its specific contents are not yet known
Admiral Cassius reported the situation to Pallod Norrim
Arriving officers said they were the only POC personnel in the area and claimed the crew must have misidentified the grav car seen leaving
The crew returned to the Regina Down TAS Hostel after the authorities arrived

The autodoc (room K, upper floor)
Same floor as the lounge, where Iaros Ujinka was shot. An autodoc is a self-contained diagnostic, pharmaceutical and surgical system the size of a large coffin — stationary and 500kg, so patients come to it, not the other way around. The crew got Ujinka into it, but the attempt came too late to revive her.





























TLAutodocSkillsWhat it adds13BasicMedic 3Diagnosis, drug delivery, surgery14ImprovedMedic 3, Science (biology) 3Reanimation, integral low berth, bioreactor that regrows limbs and organs15AdvancedMedic 4, Investigate/Science 4Fabrication chamber, tissue regeneration, simple augments, advanced sensors
Even the basic model has Medic 3, better than anyone in the party — it treats “as efficiently as a qualified doctor”.
If this one is TL14 or better, it can reanimate, provided no more than 2D minutes have passed since death. Doubled in extremely cold conditions, or extended to 1D days if the body is put in a low berth or cryoberth. Revival survival checks still apply.
Ujinka died minutes ago, one room away from it.
The house

Ground floor (right on the map) — entrance hallway, dining room, kitchen, utility room, bathroom, storerooms, holoroom, a very large library, carport, boathouse.
Upper floor (left) — lounge, study, workroom, autodoc, four bedrooms, two bathrooms, storerooms.
Worth noting for play:

A boathouse means water at the property line — a second way in, and a second way out
The carport is open to the outside; the grav car tailing the party has somewhere obvious to sit and wait
Two staircases connect the floors
The library dominates the ground floor and the study and workroom sit directly above it — this is a working scholar’s house, and whatever Ujinka wanted to discuss with Vlen Backett is likely in one of those three rooms
The autodoc is a private one, upstairs

Notes

darrian-jak.title: Darrian Jak
darrian-jak.content:
traveller sota npc
Secrets of the Ancients
Local drug dealer in Credo City.
Word on the street is that Jak sold a lot of Tusal the night Vlen Backett died. The party’s working assumption is that this is where the Tusal in Vlen’s blood came from.
Frequents a couple of back alleys around the commercial district. When the crew went there to find him, they learned the police had picked him up earlier that day.
Pallod Norrim later told Kostas Backett that the POC had arrested Jak for Vlen’s murder and confirmed that Jak is short and red-haired. That broadly matches the unseen red-haired third figure in Three Men at Vlen’s Room, but the crew have not independently established that Jak is the same person or that he killed Vlen.
Pallod treats the case as solved. The crew do not.
Jak or Harlen?
On 195-1105 Detective Odoy named the red-haired man in the case as a fixer called Harlen, connected to Winter Shipping, and said Ven Yasha — not Jak — killed Vlen.
Whether Jak and Harlen are the same person, an alias, or two different red-haired men is not established. Kept as separate notes until the table settles it.
The crew are fairly confident they are two different men, and that Jak is a fall guy — arrested purely because he is also red-haired, giving the POC a redhead to charge and close the case with. This is the crew’s inference, not proven, and it makes Pallod’s arrest look like deliberate misdirection rather than incompetence.
Notes

In POC custody; the crew asked for an opportunity to face him.
The crew plan to try to meet Jak in prison to test Pallod’s case and settle the Harlen question.

delta-2.title: Delta 2
delta-2.content:
traveller sota ship clue
Secrets of the Ancients
Ship that hailed the Event Horizon as she came out of jump at Alell, c. 219-1105: “This is Alell patrol ship Delta 2. Prepare for inspection. Please confirm.” Later “prepare for docking procedures”.
Destroyed by the Event Horizon’s missiles, Session 2026-10-04.
It wasn’t what it said it was.

Ozy’s Computers check: Alell doesn’t normally have patrol ships assigned
When Ozy asked for its security handshake and the proper ship-to-ship protocol, it cut comms and armoured up
Faster than the Event Horizon (thrust above her 2), and it came straight at her, thrusting flat out
Per the GM after the fight: a Far Trader with two weapons, a missile rack and a beam laser

The table guessed “space pirate”. The GM’s framing during the fight: it was going for a “shitty lab ship ripe for the plucking” that it probably didn’t expect to be armed. Who crewed it and who sent it is unknown. Nobody was identified and nothing was recovered.
The fight

Fired at least three salvos: one in round 1, two more in round 2 (the second launch was detected in round 3 and taken for a new one). The first, four missiles, hit in round 5 for 20 plus a 3-point Hull critical. The next two hit in round 6 after Delta 2 was already destroyed: 54 damage with three criticals, then Effect 0 for none
Its point defence knocked one missile out of the Event Horizon’s first salvo
It had the initiative in rounds 4 and 5. If it had gone first in round 6 it would have been in beam laser range, able to fire on the Event Horizon or her missiles
Took 30 damage in round 5 (Effect +2) and 28 in round 6 (Effect +3), then the damage chain and a second salvo blew it apart: “secondary, tertiary explosions… fuel lines exploding”. The hulk was obliterated

Notes

Session 2026-09-27: space combat opened at very long range. The Event Horizon fired three missiles on turn 1. (The incoming missiles reported that turn are the same salvo Kostas detected in round 1 of Session 2026-10-04, not a separate one.)
Session 2026-10-04: destroyed in round 6, without ever closing to laser range

detective-odoy.title: Detective Odoy
detective-odoy.content:
traveller sota npc
Secrets of the Ancients
Person of interest on the investigation board, alongside Pallod Norrim.
He’s the mysterious man who wants to meet the party at The Flotsam at 10pm on 195-1105 — due tonight; see Meeting at the Flotsam.
Dark unkempt hair, stubble, worn dark jacket — nothing like Norrim’s uniform. A detective who arranges meetings in a bar at night rather than summoning people to an office is either working around his own organisation or isn’t with one.
Not yet recorded: which agency he belongs to, whether he’s on Vlen Backett’s Murder, and how he got word to the party.
Appearance

What he told the crew — 195-1105
The meeting happened. Odoy is investigating Ven Yasha, and his account contradicts Pallod Norrim’s official case at every point. All of the following is Odoy’s claim and none of it is independently verified:

Ven Yasha killed Vlen Backett — not Darrian Jak, whom the POC have arrested for it
Vlen was a courier for Ven Yasha
No Zhodani spy was killed. The murder behind that rumour is Vlen’s, and he was not a spy — the spy story is a cover used to justify the Imperial police takeover of the inquiry
Imperial security have been everywhere on Regina
The Imperial force that arrived aboard the Alahir is hunting Ven Yasha
Both Dancado attackers are in Imperial hands — the prisoner is no longer in POC custody, and the Imperials also collected the dead man
The red-haired man is a fixer called Harlen, connected to Winter Shipping
He knows little about Iaros Ujinka or why she would be killed

Open questions

Which agency he serves, and what he wants from the crew — he arranged the meeting, they didn’t
Whether Pallod Norrim is bought, coerced, or simply sidelined
Whether Harlen and Darrian Jak are the same man
Why he approached this crew rather than working through his own organisation

Notes


Not updated. Kostas wanted him told about the base; the others didn’t get to him before leaving Regina on 196-1105. GM: “Detective Odoy will never know what happened. He probably wouldn’t believe you anyway”

dranxi-jungle.content:

droyne.title: Droyne
droyne.content:
traveller sota species
Secrets of the Ancients
A species found in association with The Ancients — the similarities between Ancients sites include the use of Droyne as pets or servants, which is one of the arguments for a single Ancients culture (see Ancients Extinction Theories).
They have their own social organisation: an oyntrip is a Droyne unit ranging in size from a handful of individuals to the population of a whole planet, roughly cognate to a ‘clan’ or ‘nation’. The existence of a living Droyne vocabulary says they are very much still here.
Nothing else established in play: where they are, or what they remember.
Notes

efate.title: Efate
efate.content:
traveller sota location
Secrets of the Ancients
High Tech Level, high population, almost as influential as Regina. A major crossroads for trade and Imperial naval operations — the 213th Fleet is headquartered here.
Visitors are cautioned that local customs and cultures change over short periods, and that the pace of life is uncomfortable to many. Per the Efate tourist board: live fast, die young, get resurrected by our advanced medical technology.
Uakye is closely associated with Efate, and resents it.
Notes

event-horizon.title: Event Horizon
event-horizon.content:
traveller sota ship
Secrets of the Ancients
The party’s ship. A Lab Ship. Owned by Graxius StClair — the other characters’ Ship Shares, Kostas Backett’s among them, contributed a little towards her.
Carries a Pinnace, the Implacable, which belongs to Tyrus Cassius.
She belongs to StClair. Tyrus Cassius owns the Implacable and nothing more of her.
This is the ship Kostas Backett talked his way aboard to find Cassius and demand a job.
Open decision: Iaros Ujinka has asked whether the party will put the Event Horizon behind Ujinka’s Research, in the role Vlen Backett was going to fill. No answer given yet. She’s a Lab Ship, which makes her the right hull for it.
Crew

Graxius StClair — owner
Kostas Backett
Ozymandius Forthrast
Tyrus Cassius
Talia — steward (Steward 3), Cr4,000/month from 196-1105 (was Cr2,000)
Gunner Gunnerson — gunner, Cr4,000/month
Atticus Brown — second gunner, cheap; “just wanted to get off planet”
Zed Cole — the friendly ex-passenger, joined Session 2026-10-18; Experienced Combatant, small-craft pilot; salary agreed but not set

Crew wages Cr9,000/month total from 196-1105 (was Cr7,000).
Aboard

Two research companies under charter, Helix and Black Horizon, with their own labs — off limits to passengers. Their row over a joint discovery in the first jump was settled in Black Horizon’s favour by Ozy. Charter terms now known: Helix pay the ship a 2% royalty on breakthroughs capped at Cr1,000,000; Black Horizon pay none, claim exclusive patents, and the crew may not inspect Black Horizon’s cargo — which is how live carthuses got aboard and into the maintenance shafts in the third jump. Black Horizon have their own security detail
Five High Passengers for Alell, boarded at Regina 196-1105, Cr60,000 each on arrival. Vetted on a Streetwise roll; the GM rolled their identities on a D66 table privately — and one of them is a shapeshifting alien in a skin suit, whose mating pheromone stank out the ventilation in the second jump
Maintenance shafts and ventilation run everywhere and are, as Kostas put it, exposed to everything. Repair drones can be flown through the vents on Remote Ops
Medbay: DM+1 to Medic checks, treats up to five patients
No low berths — low passage isn’t an option
12 tons of cargo space; each high passenger uses one ton
Vlen Backett’s body, transferred from the POC on Regina and carried to Alell for burial
Jump-2. Refuels by skimming gas giants (no roll needed; a roll only speeds it up)
Thrust 2, poor for a fight
Three turrets: missile, pulse (medium range) and beam (long range). One missile rack, 12 missiles, 9 left after Session 2026-09-27. Restocking costs Cr250,000. Each missile that hits does 4D6

Correction, from Rich’s armoury sheet and the rulebook: the beam laser is the Medium-range one and the pulse laser the Long-range one. All 12 missiles were spent in Session 2026-10-04. See Armoury below


Improved sensors
Armour, no shields. Nobody out here has shields

Correction, Session 2026-10-04: the GM confirmed she has no armour at all. Nothing comes off incoming damage


No dedicated mechanic or engineer. In a fight, damage control means someone swapping off a station
Quirks (she’s second-hand): nothing combat-related, just −10 Hull. Starting Hull 124
One spare hard point for another turret (a sandcaster was suggested)
Airlocks: one under the air/raft, one at the end of the docking ring where the Implacable connects, and an unspecified number around the circular section

Armoury
From Rich’s P&L sheet (Armoury tab). Three single turrets, TL7, Power 1 and 1 ton each.









































WeaponTLPowerRangeDamageTraitsGunner, Session 2026-10-04Beam Laser104Medium1Dunmanned, then a passenger for one salvoPulse Laser90Long2DGunner GunnersonMissile Rack74Special4DSmartAtticus Brown

Condition — in orbit over Alell, after the fight with Delta 2

Hull 47 of 124 (77 damage: 20, a 3-point Hull critical, then 54)
Power Plant critical, Severity 1: Power −10% (no practical effect, per the GM)
Jump Drive critical, Severity 1: DM−2 to all jump drive checks, unrepaired
Bridge critical, Severity 1: comms disabled, fixed by Ozy
Nowhere to repair her: Alell has no highport or orbital starport, and nobody aboard has the skills for Hull repairs. Whoever stays aboard to fix her misses what happens on the surface

Current tasking
In orbit over Alell, c. 219-1105, parked in the planet’s shadow out of the star’s radiation. She won her first space fight: Delta 2, a Far Trader posing as an Alell patrol, was destroyed by her missiles in Session 2026-10-04, but not before it put her at Hull 47 of 124 and damaged her jump drive. The Implacable took the Five High Passengers down to the surface. One jump of fuel, no gas giant, no highport.
Superseded: In the Alell system, c. 219-1105, turn 1 of a space fight with Delta 2, a ship claiming to be an Alell patrol. Missiles in flight both ways. One jump of fuel: Alell has no gas giant and no highport. Stations: Cassius piloting, Gunner Gunnerson and Kostas on the laser turrets, Atticus Brown on missiles, Ozy on sensors.
The carthus hunt finished in the third jump. Two carthuses got into the control room and started a cascading systems failure. Ozy fixed it before it caused a critical hit to the manoeuvre drive.
Earlier: in the third jump, Whanga → Alell, with escaped carthuses in the shafts and the crew hunting them. Route flown: Regina → Forboldn (departed 196-1105, 7 days 5 hours) → Whanga → Alell, skimming the gas giant at each stop. Skimmed Assiniboia for fuel while the crew were on Regina.
Carrying Ujinka’s research notes and the Boughene statuette and Vlen’s disks.
Earlier on 196-1105 she was in orbit around Assiniboia tracking Winter Shipping’s launch, and served as the crew’s armoury for the raid on the Winter Shipping Station — Regina’s Law Level 9 made arming on the ground impossible.
Finances
Now tracked in Ship Finances, which replaces Rich’s Google Sheet. The lines below are kept as history.

The month falls due after two jumps. Cr300,000 in passage fees at Alell puts her in the black
Declined 6 tons of advanced electronics at 110% of Cr100,000 base — which burned bridges with Regina’s legal cargo suppliers for a month

Session 2026-10-04: first space combat. Stations: Cassius pilot and captain, Kostas sensors, Ozy engineering, Gunnerson pulse laser, Atticus missiles; StClair available as an NPC. Fired all 12 missiles in four salvos of three and destroyed Delta 2. Took 77 damage and three criticals beyond the Hull one

exceedingly-discreet.title: Exceedingly Discreet
exceedingly-discreet.content:
traveller sota npc
Secrets of the Ancients
A Llellewyoly — a “Dandelion” — found working alone in a sealed environmental chamber in Winter Shipping’s closed Credo-side building, in the small hours of 196-1105.
“Exceedingly Discreet” is the title it gave when asked, not necessarily a name: “I am exceedingly discreet. What is your title at this time, strangers?” Llellewyoly hold dozens of formal titles at once, so this may be one of many.
It calls itself the brains of the operation. It works an enormous volume of data across pads and monitors on a closed system with no external route in — which is why Ozy’s remote hack of Winter Shipping found an almost empty server. It also controls the company launch’s flight path from that console.
It addresses people by titles it invents for them: “overly dressed pompous man” (Cassius), “pale-skinned smartly dressed man” (Ozy), “downtrodden depressed man” (Kostas), “unruly-haired rude scientist man” (StClair, after greeting it as a “ballsack with chicken legs”).
Appearance

The deal — 196-1105
It saw through two cover stories and responded to the truth. Purely transactional, and openly ambitious.
It gives: passage on the Winter Shipping launch and up to the company station in orbit, with the flight path set from its own console and Marid kept unaware. It suggested the launch meet the Event Horizon in orbit so the crew can arm themselves, since Credo’s Law Level 9 makes that impossible on the ground.
It gets: a guarantee that Harlen does not survive, and silence about the conversation. It intends to take over Winter Shipping itself, and offers its own ambition as the crew’s guarantee that it won’t turn them in.
What it says — all unverified

Harlen runs the company — “short-sighted and a poor tactician”, but loyal to Ven Yasha and not for turning. “He is just a man, though”
Ven Yasha hired all of them
Ven Yasha ordered Iaros Ujinka’s death. It does not understand why and says so — better understanding of Ancient technology would only raise the value of Ancient artefacts. It doesn’t question Yasha’s requests
Vlen Backett was a messenger for Ven Yasha — “he must have brought bad news, hence his demise”
It was aware of both murders
Harlen holds Vlen’s Statuette and Data Crystals — volunteered unprompted, because Kostas is Vlen’s nephew
Imperial Intelligence were on Regina in numbers, arrived aboard the Alahir, and have left; their business is concluded. The captain — name heard as “Gand Hulses”, unconfirmed — is said to hold a special portfolio in the intelligence services. It does not know whether they came for Yasha
On what Ancient technology is worth: nobody understands the secrets of The Ancients, but the potential runs to immortality, taking systems, taking the Imperium, destroying armies. It knows of no specific plan of Yasha’s
It will not discuss Ven Yasha at all — “for my own survival” — while freely offering Harlen, the hired thugs, and Imperial Intelligence

Open questions

Whether it means to honour the deal, or is arranging for the crew and Harlen to remove each other
What is on the closed system it guards
What it actually knows about Ven Yasha and is holding back
Whether it is a willing employee or, as StClair wondered, effectively a prisoner

Notes



Gone — 196-1105
Cassius and Ozy returned to the Credo office the morning after the base was destroyed. It was no longer there. Its sealed chamber was empty, the computers gave nothing, and nothing indicated where it had gone. Whether it knows the base is gone, or left because of it, is unknown. The crew left Regina without finding it

The earlier, Vilani-era Imperium that preceded the Third Imperium.

Alell’s starport dates back to it, and is considered an excellent example of fin-de-siècle Vilani design

five-high-passengers.title: Five High Passengers
five-high-passengers.content:
traveller sota npc
Secrets of the Ancients
The five high passengers the Event Horizon took on at Regina on 196-1105 for Alell, Cr60,000 each on safe arrival. Vetted by Cassius on Streetwise and declared “so on the level you don’t even need a spirit level”; the GM then rolled each of them on a D66 table, privately. Gunner Gunnerson looked them over and called the crew stupid.
What Talia’s headcount in the second jump turned up, none of them named yet:

The drunk — passed out when checked
The recluse — has quietly kept to their stateroom since leaving Regina
The noble — “rich noble twat”, haunting the ship like he owns it
The friendly one — overly friendly, chatting to everyone, “seeing how things work”, wanting to be part of everything. Unremarked on at the table, but worth watching
The blob — a shapeshifting alien of an unnamed species that lives in a skin suit. Its reproductive cycle hit mid-voyage; it left the suit, set up in the ventilation as a mass of pulsating goo and filled the ship with a mating pheromone that made everything smell and taste of childhood. Identified by DNA match between goo and suit. Back in its suit it was sheepish, apologised, and hid in its stateroom for the rest of the trip. Can speak while suited. Still paying

They can roam the ship but not the research labs. Each uses a ton of cargo space.

g-band-transmissions.title: G-Band Transmissions
g-band-transmissions.content:
traveller sota clue
Secrets of the Ancients
The subject of Ujinka’s Research: Iaros Ujinka is investigating links between g-band transmissions and sites of Ancient technology.
What they are — from Ujinka’s notes, 196-1105
It’s not a transmission so much as an absence of one. Standard subspace telemetry in the G-band (Ujinka’s log puts it at 4.2 GHz) suffers a sharp, recursive drop-off near Ancient sites — not solar radiation, not iron ore, but something that mimics a low-frequency multi-phasic dampening field. Ujinka reads it as the passive footprint of active “Monadium structures” buried deep in a world’s mantle.
The method: map hidden sites by the communication dead zones they cast across a system, rather than by looking for ruins.
Where the footprint has been found:

The Regina sub-sector — the 1102 survey, around the Boughene and Regina precursor ruins
Boughene, at the metal-rich asteroid belt around Boughene IV — sensor packet degradation and a 0.03-second clock-drift on the navigation computers. A statue pulled from that belt is a fragment of a larger anchor array, and is now aboard the Event Horizon (Vlen’s Statuette and Data Crystals)

Ujinka had a g-band sensor system of her own. Vlen Backett’s disks contain his reminder to acquire it and scan Boughene with it. Whether that sensor system still exists, and where, is unknown.
Juni is pursuing the signals at the Ancients site on Beck’s World now.
Notes

graxius-stclair.title: Graxius StClair
graxius-stclair.content:
traveller sota character
Secrets of the Ancients
Player character. Owns the Event Horizon — though the other characters’ Ship Shares contributed a little towards her.
Connections

Mentor — Iaros Ujinka, who was very supportive of him. She later went off to work with his ex-wife.
Ex-wife — Juni. Ujinka went to work with her, and she is still on Beck’s World, investigating the g-band signals at the Ancients site there. StClair reacted when her name came up in Ujinka’s notes on 196-1105.

Appearance

Older man, wild grey hair, wire-rimmed glasses, unshaven. Battered pale canvas coat over layered work clothes, festooned with straps, pouches, tools and a heavy satchel. Scuffed boots. Holding a book or slate. Looks like someone who works with his hands and hasn’t slept indoors much lately.
Notes

With the sniper possibly still outside after the attack at Dancado, StClair and Kostas Backett entered the exposed lounge to retrieve his mentor Iaros Ujinka. As they entered, they saw a grav car flying away and thought it bore POC colours, though they could not confirm it.
StClair and Kostas got Ujinka to the autodoc, but it was too late to revive her. StClair then treated Kostas’s injuries and restored 1 END.
Sat out the raid on the Winter Shipping Station on 196-1105 — went back to the Event Horizon in a mood to do research instead, leaving the boarding party as its two weakest fighters plus a hired gunner. He did hand Kostas a medikit on the way out, which Kostas then burned on a failed self-treatment. StClair needs to buy a new one.
196-1105: operated on Kostas in the Event Horizon’s medbay (Medic 2, medbay DM+1) and succeeded — END from 1 to 5. Did it while “up to his ass in research” and still mourning Ujinka. Spending the jump to Forboldn on research; the GM hinted something may come of it
Transit to Alell (Session 2026-09-20), player absent: pulled out of his lab for the ventilation smell, “hair even crazier than normal, I can’t work like this”. Flew a repair drone through the vents on Remote Ops (Effect +3) and found the pulsating goo; Medic check identified the pheromone; a plain Science check (his only speciality is Psionicology) worked out it was a mating cycle that would pass in days. His stun stick went to Kostas for the carthus hunt. Skills noted at the table: Computers, Remote Ops, Science (Psionicology), Streetwise, Recon, Investigate, Medic
Session 2026-09-27, player absent: “appeared out of the shadows” to use the medikit on the downed Kostas, then operated on him again in the medbay: DM+1, plus a boon die for having just done the same operation, Effect +3. Medic 2 per the table
Session 2026-10-04, player absent: offered as an NPC for the space fight, on comms or repairs. The table checked his sheet: Computers and Remote Ops, no Electronics (sensors), so no electronic warfare. Hailing Delta 2 with a warning was suggested for him; no sign it happened
Session 2026-10-18, player back: caught up on the damage to his ship and wants to dock the Admiral’s pay over it. Went down in a bright pink hazmat suit with a dagger and his stealth dagger. At Vaca Goya he studied and quietly picked the local plants (Investigate, Profession, Survival), finding “some interesting plants”. The GM will tell him privately which are poisonous or useful, so they’re contraband he’s carrying. Told Marisa and Bard they looked like husband and wife; she warmed to him until she heard his SOC (“Hermit”, −4 as said at the table). Hugged Aail and sat on a bench in bliss, then realised he may have contaminated her with plant sap, and kept quiet. His line on paying: the ship goes nowhere unless he presses the button

gunner-gunnerson.title: Gunner Gunnerson
gunner-gunnerson.content:
traveller sota npc
Secrets of the Ancients
The Event Horizon’s gunner. Brought along as hired muscle for the raid on the Winter Shipping Station on 196-1105, when StClair pulled out and the boarding party was down to its two worst combatants.
Arrived with the line “did someone call for backup?”
Rolled up as an elite NPC and it showed — both firefights aboard the base turned on his shooting, and the GM downgraded his laser rifle to a laser carbine mid-session after a single aimed shot did 35 damage and obliterated a man from the waist up.
Run at the table by Kostas’ player as a second character.
Appearance

Grizzled older man, close-cropped grey hair, heavy stubble, one eye ruined and scarred over. Filthy dark boiler suit patched with unit tags and stuffed with tools and pouches, sleeves rolled, work gloves at the belt. Chews a cigar throughout. Battered boots.
Manner
Former Marine and still fighting like one. Falls into hand signals none of the crew can read, takes point without being asked, and shoots rather than talks — no warnings, no hands up. Delivers one-liners over the bodies.
Stealth −4. He does not sneak.
He is also the only member of the boarding party who did anything medical: he broke off mid-firefight to bandage Kostas for a point of END after Kostas’ own first aid failed, and later dragged him bodily to the escape capsules.
Notes

Killed both men on the base’s dock level, and at least two more of the smugglers above
Took a parting shot at the last surviving smuggler as the escape capsule launched, purely because he could
196-1105: took Kostas and the statuette and disks straight back to the Event Horizon from the landing site. Paid Cr4,000/month; a performance bonus was discussed, not decided. Regaling the ship with his deeds on the base — shin still sore from where the Admiral kicked him, which shook a spare clip out of his pocket. Looked the new passengers over and told the crew they were stupid
Session 2026-09-27: on one of the laser turrets for the space fight with Delta 2
Session 2026-10-04: on the pulse laser (Gunner +2). Delta 2 never came into range for a shot. Tried point defence against two incoming salvos (2D6+2, 8+) and missed both. “Someone order a backup?” Afterwards he folded his arms at the captain and told him not to mention money “after I save your scrawny ass”

harlen.title: Harlen
harlen.content:
traveller sota npc
Secrets of the Ancients
A fixer, red-haired, who ran Winter Shipping for Ven Yasha. Seen in person for the first time on 196-1105, aboard the company’s hidden base — and last seen there as it counted down to destruction.
Originally named by Detective Odoy at the Meeting at the Flotsam on 195-1105 as the red-haired man in the case, then confirmed from inside the company by Exceedingly Discreet.
196-1105 — aboard the base
He arrived late into the firefight on the upper level, shot at Gunner Gunnerson and missed, and began shouting to rally his remaining people.
Then he saw Kostas. His expression changed and he muttered “oh” — he had only registered the others until that point. He looked across at Cassius’ uniform, said “This is suboptimal”, and closed his eyes.
Every screen in the base went black. An alarm sounded and a synthesised voice announced destruct sequence activated, detonation imminent, all hands to re-entry capsules, with floor lights marking a path to the capsule airlock. Thirty seconds. He stood there with his eyes shut through it.
He legged it before Kostas could order him taken alive. Ozy, opening doors on the way to the capsules, found him sat at his desk, eyes closed, fingers steepled, muttering “this is not the end” over and over. Ozy took the statuette and data disks off the desk and left him there.
Nobody saw him board a capsule and nobody saw him die. The base was destroyed roughly twenty seconds after the crew launched.
He controls things without touching them
The station obeyed him with no console, no keypad and no spoken command — he shut his eyes and the screens died and the destruct ran. This is not explained. Candidates: psionics (see Zhodani, and the Imperium’s attitude to psionic talent), a neural implant tied into the base’s systems, or something to do with The Ancients.
Worth setting against The Device carried by the third man at Dancado, which caused electrical interference nobody could account for, and against the localised systems failures Kostas asked Pallod Norrim about and was told were coincidence.
He knew the crew on sight
He recognised Kostas without being told who he was, and recognised Cassius’ uniform. Either the company was briefed on who was coming, or he had seen Vlen’s family before — Kostas is Vlen’s nephew and next of kin.
From inside the company — 196-1105
Per Exceedingly Discreet, the Llellewyoly running Winter Shipping’s records, all unverified:

Harlen ran the company, and Ven Yasha hired them all
Short-sighted and a poor tactician, but loyal to Ven Yasha and not for turning
No particular weakness — “he is just a man, though”
He held Vlen’s Statuette and Data Crystals — volunteered unprompted, because Kostas is Vlen’s nephew

Exceedingly Discreet wanted Harlen dead and the company for itself, and made that the price of flying the crew up. The crew agreed to kill him. In the event the base blew up with him apparently still in it — which satisfies the deal only by assumption, and Exceedingly Discreet does not yet know any of it.
Possible identity with Darrian Jak
Pallod Norrim arrested short, red-haired Darrian Jak for Vlen Backett’s murder and treats the case as closed. Odoy names the red-haired man as Harlen and says Ven Yasha is the killer.
The crew’s working theory: Harlen and Jak are not the same man. Jak is a fall guy, arrested purely because he is also red-haired and was conveniently to hand — which would make Harlen the real third man in Three Men at Vlen’s Room and Pallod’s case a deliberate misdirection. Nothing seen aboard the base settles this either way; Jak is still in POC custody and Harlen was never questioned.
Open questions

Is he dead? “This is not the end” is not the line of a man expecting to die
How did he run the station without touching it?
Was he the third man at Vlen’s room, or at Dancado?
Why was the statuette on his desk rather than passed up to Ven Yasha?
Is he the same man as Darrian Jak?
What “this is not the end” refers to

Notes

helix.title: Helix
helix.content:
traveller sota faction
Secrets of the Ancients
One of two research companies chartering lab space aboard the Event Horizon, the other being Black Horizon. Their labs are off limits to passengers.
Two or three days into the jump from Regina to Forboldn, a discovery was made combining Helix equipment with Black Horizon research, and the two teams fell into a blazing row over ownership, patents and royalties. Talia asked the crew to intervene. Settled against them: Ozy’s analysis of the logs (Computers, Effect +4 — he chose the outcome) showed the discovery was Black Horizon’s, and Black Horizon’s contract gives them exclusive patent rights with no royalties. Helix are pissed off but bound.
Their charter terms (per Ozy’s read): genuinely honest, painfully bureaucratic, red tape everywhere; the ship gets a 2% royalty on breakthroughs, capped at Cr1,000,000.
Their rep aboard is played with a hyena picture: Rok (heard as “Rock Anlo”; the portrait filename spells it Rok).
Nothing else known about the company or what it researches.

Full name, per the logo and their rep’s lab coat: Helix Advanced Materials.

Session 2026-09-27: warned by Ozy about Delta 2’s “inspection” at Alell. They started preparing their documentation, “of which there is a lot”

henna-backett.title: Henna Backett
henna-backett.content:
traveller sota npc alell
Secrets of the Ancients
Kostas’s mother, of the Backett Family in Vaca Goya on Alell. Married to Merrick Backett. Name confirmed by Rich after Session 2026-10-18.

Session 2026-10-18: at Vlen’s homecoming. She went straight to the Admiral’s side: “Oh Admiral, it’s so good to see you again.” She hoped her boy was doing his duty, and that his coffee was to the Admiral’s liking. When the Admiral said it had been poor lately: “Shouldn’t have got shot then, really, should you, boy?” Later she told Kostas not to leave the Admiral alone, and to make sure he gets what he needs. “Again” suggests she has met Cassius before; nothing at the table explained when.

iaros-ujinka.title: Iaros Ujinka
iaros-ujinka.content:
traveller sota npc
Secrets of the Ancients


                  
                  Dead 
                  
                

Shot through a window at Dancado during her meeting with the party, and killed. Shooter unseen. The attack cut the power and destroyed the house’s security drone.
Second person connected to Ujinka’s Research murdered inside four days. The first was Vlen Backett.
The crew got her to the autodoc upstairs at Dancado, but it was too late to revive her.


Professor Iaros Ujinka, Department of History, University of Regina. Lives at Dancado, an estate just outside Credo City.
Graxius StClair’s mentor — she was very supportive of him. At some point she went off to work with StClair’s ex-wife, which appears to be a sore subject.
The party met her at Dancado after being followed there by a grav car apparently in POC colours — see Being Followed. She was murdered during that meeting.
Her work, and what she wanted from Vlen, is in Ujinka’s Research: links between G-Band Transmissions and sites of Ancient technology. Before her death, she asked whether the party would put the Event Horizon behind it. No answer given yet.
On Ven Yasha — whose name kept cropping up in connection with Vlen — she knows him only by reputation, and says he is very unpleasant.
The letter
Found among Vlen Backett’s effects, addressed to him care of the Regina Down TAS Hostel:

I have returned from Beck’s World, and am now available for that meeting we discussed at your convenience. If you would care to visit me at my home on Dancado, I shall be delighted to receive you and discuss topics of mutual interest.

This is the lead that sent the party to Dancado.
What it establishes

Vlen and Ujinka already knew each other and had a meeting arranged before Vlen ever reached Regina — “that meeting we discussed”
The “topics of mutual interest” turn out to be Ujinka’s Research — Vlen was to provide funding and a ship
Ujinka had been away on Beck’s World and had only just got back
A drifter with no visible profession was corresponding with a university historian — which fits Vlen’s dabbling in archaeology and his unnamed contacts among scientists
Vlen may well have been on Regina for this meeting. He never made it.

Open questions

Whether anyone else knew about the meeting — the letter was sitting in a hostel room that three men walked into
Whether she knew Vlen and StClair were connected, or whether two of her contacts turning up in the same story is coincidence
How much she knew about where Vlen’s money came from
Why Ven Yasha’s name attaches to Vlen at all

Who ordered it â€” 196-1105
Exceedingly Discreet says Ven Yasha ordered Ujinka’s death. Unverified, but it comes from inside Yasha’s own organisation and is the first account of her murder from anyone â€” Detective Odoy had none.
The same source finds it inexplicable: better understanding of Ancient technology would only raise the value of Ancient artefacts, so killing the academic studying it makes no commercial sense. The crew speculated she may have intended to keep the technology out of the wrong hands, or use it herself â€” speculation only.
Notes

Ozy recovered three research notes from her computer — transcribed in Ujinka’s Research. They name Juni as the colleague carrying the work on at Beck’s World, and record Vlen borrowing the Boughene statue from her.
She had a g-band sensor system of her own; Vlen meant to acquire it.

imperium.title: Imperium
imperium.content:
traveller sota faction
Secrets of the Ancients
The setting’s dominant polity — formally the Third Imperium. Official documents are dated by its regnal year: Handout 2 is sealed “190 Standard, in the 1105th year of the Third Imperium”.
The Imperial Calendar numbers days within the year — 190-1105, 193-1105 — and names weekdays; 193-1105 is a Thirday. Campaign present is 193-1105. Vargr from outside the Imperium once travelled hundreds of parsecs to consult Vlen Backett — so there’s a meaningful outside, and Vlen has business in it.
Presumably the same navy Kostas Backett was drafted into and Tyrus Cassius and Aylin Boro served in, though nothing has said so outright yet.
Notes

implacable.content:
traveller sota ship

Pinnace carried by the Event Horizon. Owned by Tyrus Cassius.
