Kostas Backett is still at STR 3, DEX 9, END 1. StClair has been sick and has a plastic knife
Iaros Ujinka’s request that the Event Horizon back Ujinka’s Research is still unanswered

Priorities for next session

Arm the crew — rendezvous with the Event Horizon in orbit and get real weapons aboard before the station
Take the launch to the Winter Shipping Station — deal with the staff, find Harlen
Recover Vlen’s Statuette and Data Crystals from Harlen
Decide how far to honour the deal — the crew have promised a killing, and Exceedingly Discreet keeps its own counsel about Ven Yasha

session-2026-09-06.title: Session 2026-09-06
session-2026-09-06.content:
traveller sota session
Secrets of the Ancients
Session date: 2026-09-06
In-fiction date: 196-1105, from the small hours through to the morning
Starting position
The crew are inside Winter Shipping’s closed Credo-side office in the small hours of 196-1105, deal struck with Exceedingly Discreet: passage up to the company’s orbital base in exchange for Harlen’s death.

The route up is arranged — the company launch, flight path set from Exceedingly Discreet’s console, Marid unaware
The crew have no weapons; Regina is Law Level 9
Kostas Backett is badly injured at STR 3, DEX 9, END 1
Vlen’s Statuette and Data Crystals are said to be in Harlen’s hands, aboard the base

Live notes

StClair sat the raid out. He went back to the Event Horizon in a mood to do research, leaving the two least effective combat characters to board a hostile installation. He handed Kostas a medikit on the way out
The Implacable had already returned to the Event Horizon — its mooring fees at Regina Highport were only paid so far. It met the launch in orbit as planned and the crew armed there
Backup: Gunner Gunnerson, the Event Horizon’s gunner — a grizzled ex-Marine in a filthy boiler suit, chewing a cigar, rolled up as elite. Announced himself with “did someone call for backup?” Run by Kostas’ player as a second character. Stealth −4; he does not sneak
The base is not a station. The launch flew out to a semi-stable Lagrangian point between Regina and Assiniboia, into a container yard — thousands of cargo containers docked into long lines and cubes, some drifting free and untethered, nav buoys and warning beacons among them. The launch dipped beneath a trio of old containers, a concealed hatch opened, and it docked inside
Interior: three shipping containers bolted together. No lights anywhere — the staff know their way around in the dark. Doors barely airtight, everything cobbled together. The dock bay held only the launch and a few sealed crates
First firefight — the dock level. Gunnerson took point, opened the door and got a surprise round on a man standing with his back turned, mid-conversation with someone in the toilet

Gunnerson’s opening shot tore into his back for 19 and left him at END 0, still standing
Kostas fired Vlen’s gun for 9 once the laser sight and P-HUD bonuses were found — the table spent a while working out that the sheet wasn’t including them
Ozy leaned through the doorway at −1 and hit the ceiling
Cassius rolled Leadership for Effect 5 — five DM+1 tokens to hand out over the fight, and they carried most of the party’s hits
Gunnerson aimed and finished him for 35 damage, at which point the GM retconned his laser rifle down to a carbine for being wildly overpowered. Reduced to 27; the man’s top half was obliterated
The second man burst out of the toilet still pulling his trousers up. Kostas shot him for 15 — “this one’s for the Admiral” — the Effect wiping out his protection entirely. He was flung back into the toilet, dropped his gun and slipped in the mess. Cassius finished him with the machine gun
The bodies yielded a stub pistol and some cigarettes. Nothing else


The machine gun was loud. Movement was heard on the floor above, reached by an airlock and ladder
Second firefight — the upper level. A long cover fight against the base’s smugglers, most shots hitting cover rather than people. Gunnerson went up first, called down that he could see two or three, and fought from cover the whole way

Ozy missed repeatedly, then discovered his damage dice were configured wrong on Roll20 — rolling a flat +3 instead of 3D6. Corrected mid-fight
One smuggler charged out, slipped on his mate’s corpse and went prone at −6. Kostas gut-shot him dead
Cassius came up, dropped one with the Gauss rifle for 9 through no cover, and another later with a body shot
Kostas was shot for 3 through his flak jacket (Protection 5) — enough to take END to 0 and put him on STR. He was hit again shortly after


Kostas’ self-treatment failed. With no doctor in reach, he used StClair’s medikit (TL10, DM+1) on himself and rolled Effect −4. The GM checked the rules, found nothing that defines the consequence of a failed first aid, and homeruled it: no characteristics regained, no further damage — “killing yourself with a third medic roll is insane” — and the medikit is spent. StClair owes himself a new one
Gunnerson later broke off to bandage Kostas for 1 point, taken on END
Harlen appeared. A red-haired man, arriving late into the fight. He shot at Gunnerson and missed, then began shouting to rally his people

Then he saw Kostas — and his expression changed. He muttered “oh”. He looked across at the Admiral’s uniform, said “This is suboptimal”, and closed his eyes
Every screen in the base went black. An alarm sounded and a synthesised voice announced: destruct sequence activated, detonation imminent, all hands to re-entry capsules. Floor lights lit a path of white arrows to an airlock, which popped open
Thirty seconds to detonation. Harlen simply stood there with his eyes closed


The crew debated staying to grab something versus running. Cassius made the executive decision to go. Kostas wanted Harlen taken alive — “shoot him in the legs, Gunner” — reasoning he wouldn’t blow a station he was still standing on. Harlen legged it before anyone could act on it
The launch was never an escape route. It was on an automated flight path controlled remotely by Exceedingly Discreet, and had already detached. The only way off was the escape capsules
Down at the capsule deck the surviving smugglers were trying the hatches; the first two were locked and jammed. Kostas ran past them and a capsule lit green and opened — big enough for five. He held it and waved his gun at anyone approaching
Ozy went door-to-door on the way out. One door opened onto what looked like the base’s gun emplacement. The next opened onto Harlen at his desk — eyes closed, fingers steepled, muttering “this is not the end” over and over

On the desk: a statuette Ozy recognised as the same sort of thing that was in Professor Ujinka’s house, and a set of data disks
He grabbed both and ran. He did not touch Harlen


Gunnerson killed a smuggler at the capsules and took a parting shot at the last one as the capsule launched. The crew left the final smuggler alive, still trying to force a jammed hatch
The base died about twenty seconds out — imploded, scrunched up, then blew outward. The capsule rode the edge of the wave, guided itself down, and landed in wild land on the outskirts of the Twin Cities on Regina. Grav bikes were waiting at what looked like a designated recovery point
GM: “You’ve completed Chapter 1.”

Decisions and discoveries

Vlen’s Statuette and Data Crystals are recovered — the party’s stated objective for the raid, achieved in the last thirty seconds of it. Presumed Vlen’s on strong circumstantial grounds; nobody in the fiction confirmed it
The statuette resembles Iaros Ujinka’s Ancient material. The first physical object linking Vlen, Ujinka’s Research and Ven Yasha’s organisation
The “station” was a hidden base — three containers bolted together, buried in a Lagrangian container yard, unlit and unregistered. It is destroyed.
Harlen triggered the self-destruct by closing his eyes. Screens blacked out and the station obeyed him with no console, no keypad and no spoken command. Psionics, an implant, or something else is not established — but the GM flagged his red hair repeatedly and gave him “this is not the end” as an exit line
Harlen recognised Kostas on sight, and recognised Cassius’ uniform. He knew who they were before they said a word
Harlen’s fate is unknown. He was last seen at his desk as the countdown ran, and the base was destroyed. Nobody saw him board a capsule and nobody saw him die. The promise to Exceedingly Discreet is fulfilled only by assumption
Gunner Gunnerson carried the fight. Both firefights turned on his shooting, and he twice broke off to drag or patch Kostas
The failed medic check is now settled as a house rule: no gain, no extra harm, equipment consumed

End position

Morning of 196-1105, standing in wild land outside the Twin Cities on Regina with grav bikes available and a ride back into the city
Kostas Backett at roughly STR 1, DEX 2, END 1 — three damaged characteristics, needs surgery, and cannot heal on rest. The Event Horizon’s sickbay is the fix
The party hold a statuette and data disks neither of them has examined
Winter Shipping’s orbital base, its records of whatever moved through it, and most of its staff are gone. Exceedingly Discreet is still at its console in Credo, and does not yet know
Iaros Ujinka’s request that the Event Horizon back Ujinka’s Research is still unanswered

Priorities for next session

Get Kostas into surgery — the ship’s sickbay, or a Regina hospital
Examine the statuette and the data disks — the first material from Vlen’s own hands
Establish whether Harlen is dead, and what he actually was
Face Exceedingly Discreet — its company just exploded, and the crew were the last people aboard
Still open and deprioritised: Darrian Jak in prison, Detective Odoy’s motives, The Device

session-2026-09-13.title: Session 2026-09-13
session-2026-09-13.content:
traveller sota session
Secrets of the Ancients
Session date: 2026-09-13
In-fiction date: 196-1105, morning — then two or three days into jump
GM’s framing: an in-between-chapters session — take on passengers for the next trip, tidy loose ends, then downtime in jump for training. Delivered as promised: trade and passenger rolls, a surgery, a lore drop, and a jump. “A bit bitty, but you’re on your way.”
Starting position
Morning of 196-1105, in wild land outside the Twin Cities on Regina with grav bikes and a ride back into the city. Chapter 1 complete; the base is destroyed.

Kostas Backett at STR 1 · DEX 2 · END 1 — needs surgery (failed surgery costs 3 + Effect more; at STR 1 that’s lethal). Ship’s sickbay or a Regina hospital
Vlen’s Statuette and Data Crystals in hand, unexamined
Harlen’s fate unknown — “this is not the end”
Exceedingly Discreet does not yet know its base is gone
Iaros Ujinka’s request that the Event Horizon back Ujinka’s Research still unanswered
StClair’s medikit is spent
Vlen’s body and estate still with the POC; Kostas is next of kin

Prep notes

Get Kostas to a hospital, he needs surgery (medic check, p.82)

Ask about Slow Drug
Get END to 7 (max), then…
Medical care on the ship: 3 + END DM (0) + doctor’s medical skill per day
5 days max to get back to normal


Examine the statuette, read the data disks
Decide where we’re going, get trade and passengers

Careful with the passengers, we’ve caused a bit of trouble on Regina


Confront Exceedingly Discreet - what wasn’t he telling us about Harlen?
Where is Vlen’s body right now? I should probably do something with that
Training in downtime

x8 weeks of 8hrs/day
EDU check (8+)



Live notes

Split up at the landing site. The crew were still carrying weapons they’re not allowed to hold on Law Level 9 Regina, and Kostas was bleeding out. Gunnerson took Kostas straight back up to the Event Horizon along with the statuette and the data disks; Cassius and Ozy went back into Credo to tie up loose ends. Cover story if asked: they’d gone exploring outside the city and been ambushed. Cassius offered up his own savings to cover whatever the trip needed
Kostas suggested from his sickbed that the others find Detective Odoy and give him an update — “let him keep causing more trouble for Ven Yasha”. It didn’t happen. GM: “Detective Odoy will never know what happened. He probably wouldn’t believe you anyway”
Winter Shipping’s Credo office — a dead end. Cassius and Ozy went back in. Exceedingly Discreet was gone — “the daffodil guy” is no longer in its sealed chamber, and nothing in the building indicated where it went. Ozy’s one good Recon roll of the campaign turned up a receipt for the trade the crew did with Winter Shipping earlier — something they already knew about — and nothing else; the computers gave nothing. They were making the neighbours suspicious, so they left on a cover story about a package in transit being with a different courier. Ideas about checking shipping/taxi companies or finding where Dandelions congregate were floated and dropped: “this feels like a dead end”. Back up to the Highport on the hourly shuttle
Destination: Alell — Vlen’s homeworld and the Backetts’, and where his body is to be buried. The GM noted Kostas is from Roup and that Ozy’s homeworld is Uakye, “right next door to Alell”
Route. The Event Horizon is Jump-2, so Alell is three jumps minimum, about three weeks: Regina → Forboldn (two parsecs) → Whanga → Alell. Passengers could be sought for three destinations at two, four and five parsecs. Cassius asked for a pit stop at Barbag; the GM confirmed these are the real map names, not made up to sound rude
Passengers. The ship’s steward, Talia (Steward 3), rolled for high passage to Alell: Steward +3, high passage −4, starport A +5 (heard as), population/destination modifiers, came out at 11 people wanting high passage to Alell. Cassius’s idea of auctioning tickets to the highest bidder was withdrawn when the GM said a bad Streetwise roll would lose passengers. GM first ruled double occupancy for ten, then re-read the rule: high passage is one per stateroom, so five. Middle passage the same, basic passage two to a room. Five high passengers to Alell at Cr60,000 each = Cr300,000 if they arrive safely

Vetting. Nobody has Investigate. Cassius rolled Streetwise and the table declared the passengers “fantastic people… so on the level you don’t even need a spirit level” while describing them as Jeffrey Dahmer and Fred West lookalikes. The GM then rolled on a D66 table for each of the five, privately: “Now I know who your high passengers are. And you guys don’t.” Gunnerson looked them over and called the crew stupid. Kostas was in the medbay and saw none of it
Passengers can roam the ship but not the research labs or delicate areas
Each high passenger uses a ton of cargo space; the ship has 12 tons. Low passage was considered but the Event Horizon has no low berths


Cargo. Ozy (Broker 1) rolled for incidental cargo: 15 lots available, two rolled at 6 tons and 4 tons. The 6-ton lot was advanced electronics, base Cr100,000; the supplier wanted 110% and Ozy’s broker roll couldn’t beat it. Declined — and by refusing, the crew have burned their bridges with Regina’s legal suppliers for a month. GM hinted at other, less legal suppliers; the crew voted passengers over cargo instead
Finances. Kostas’s spreadsheet first said Cr236,000 a month in costs and Cr148,000 short; he then found a subtotal error — the ship was actually only Cr33,500 short for the month before this trip, having made Cr70,000 from passengers to Regina and Cr18,000 on the Regina cargo. The month falls due after two jumps; with Cr300,000 in passage fees the ship is in the black. GM: “You can’t pay late. Well, you can — you’ll just have people after you”
Fuel. The lab ship sat skimming Assiniboia while the crew were on Regina. No roll is needed to skim, only to do it faster; Forboldn and Whanga both have gas giants, so the route can be flown on free fuel
Crew pay. A Perception check (an easy 6) showed Talia was pissed off at five passengers landing on her while paid Cr2,000 a month — “Talia the underpaid”. Ozy knew the figure. The crew doubled her to Cr4,000; she went “from not trusting you to mildly suspicious”. Gunnerson is on Cr4,000 and the crew talked about a performance bonus for keeping them alive — undecided. The second gunner, Atticus Brown, is cheap: he just wanted off-planet. Crew wages now Cr9,000 a month from Cr7,000
Kostas’s surgery. Done in the Event Horizon’s medbay (DM+1, treats up to five patients) by StClair, Medic 2, total DM+3, “up to his ass in research” and still mourning Ujinka. Succeeded — END up from 1 to 5. Kostas plans the daily medical care from there: END to 7 and DEX up on day one, DEX to full on day two, STR sorted two days after. Two days of healing already banked by session end
The lore drop. The GM shared three of Ujinka’s research notes, recovered by Ozy from her computer at Dancado — see that note for the text — and described the statuette and disks:

The statuette is a winged pillar of an ivory-like substance. Scanned with the ship’s sensors: a work of art, not a technological device. All evidence points to it being of Ancients origin
It is the statue from Research Note 2 — the one a trader pulled from the asteroid belt in the Boughene system, which Ujinka’s margin note says Vlen asked to borrow “for analysis by one of his contacts”. Vlen somehow got hold of it; the disks corroborate the match
The disks cover the Boughene asteroid belt and the g-band fluctuations described in Note 2, and include a note from Vlen reminding himself to acquire the Professor’s g-band sensor system and use it to scan the Boughene system
Note 1 is about the g-band “dead zone” method, and names Juni — StClair’s ex-wife — as taking the work to the Ancients site on Beck’s World. StClair reacted to her name
GM’s plain-English gloss: unnatural interference on a band nobody at the table understands, which Ujinka — and Vlen — thought was a way to track down remaining Ancient sites, “and maybe the secrets of the Ancients”


The Event Horizon is in one piece: the two research companies aboard, Helix and Black Horizon, “haven’t killed each other”, and Talia reported a quiet few days. Gunnerson is regaling anyone who’ll listen about his deeds on the base — his shin is still sore from where the Admiral kicked him, though it did shake an extra clip of ammo out of his pocket
Jump to Forboldn. Cassius ran the ship computer: astrogation succeeded with Effect +1, jump drive roll came up +6. “Off to hell!” — 7 days 5 hours in jump. D100 for random encounters came up clear
Downtime. Cassius is training — Investigate was the joke, “some fucking thing we haven’t got” — and needs eight weeks of it. StClair is researching; the GM hinted something might come of it. Using a skill at the table does not count towards training it
Cliffhanger, second or third morning in jump. Talia came onto the bridge with a stern face: “I’m going to need your help on something.” A discovery has been made combining Helix equipment with Black Horizon research, and the two teams are in a blazing row over who owns it — patents, royalties, ownership. The passengers haven’t caught wind yet. Ozy intends to settle it with Advocate — he claims the charter contract has a clause defaulting disputed joint discoveries to the carrier, i.e. the ship; GM: “good try, we’ll see”. A well-thought-out approach may earn a Boon. Parked for next session

Decisions and discoveries

The ship is bound for Alell, three jumps out, carrying five high passengers of unknown character. Vlen’s home, his family, and his burial. Route Forboldn → Whanga → Alell; first leg under way
Exceedingly Discreet has gone. No trace at the Credo office. It knows its base is gone or it doesn’t; either way it’s no longer where the crew can reach it. The Winter Shipping thread on Regina is closed for now
Detective Odoy was not told anything. The crew left Regina without reporting back to anyone
The statuette is Ancient, is art, and came from Boughene’s asteroid belt — the trader’s find in Ujinka’s Note 2, which Vlen “borrowed”. It’s a fragment of what Ujinka called a larger anchor array. This is the first physical link between Vlen, Ujinka’s g-band work and a specific system
Vlen intended to scan Boughene with Ujinka’s g-band sensor system — the disks say so in his own words. His funding-and-a-ship offer had a target
Ujinka’s Research now has text. Three notes: the g-band dead-zone method (Note 1), the Boughene log and the statue (Note 2), and the Deneb conference claim that the Ancients were a single unified entity that “engineered the very matter to resist time” (Note 3)
StClair’s ex-wife is Juni, and she is working the Ancients site on Beck’s World right now
Regina’s legal cargo suppliers are closed to the crew for a month
Kostas is out of danger — surgery succeeded, END 5 and climbing
Rules settled at the table: high/middle passage is one passenger per stateroom; each high passenger consumes a ton of cargo space; skimming needs no roll; a failed surgery costs 3 + Effect (confirmed from p.82 but not tested); skill use doesn’t count as training

End position

Two or three days into a 7-day jump from Regina to Forboldn, first of three legs to Alell
Five high passengers aboard, vetted by vibes; the GM knows who they are
A patent row between Helix and Black Horizon is boiling on the lab decks; Talia has asked the crew to intervene
Kostas Backett at END 5, DEX and STR still damaged, on daily medical care from StClair; expected back to full within about four days
Cassius two days into eight weeks of training
Cr300,000 due on arrival at Alell; the month’s Cr33,500 shortfall is covered by it. Crew wages Cr9,000
Harlen still unaccounted for. Exceedingly Discreet vanished. Detective Odoy uninformed. Vlen’s body still on Regina with the POC — the crew left without it

Correction, 2026-10-18: Rich confirms the crew had Vlen’s body transferred to the ship before leaving Regina. It came with them and is with them at Alell.


Ujinka’s Research: still no formal answer to her request, but the ship is carrying her notes, her statue, and Vlen’s plan to scan Boughene

Priorities for next session

Settle the Helix / Black Horizon dispute — Ozy’s Advocate roll, with the carrier clause as his line; think out the approach for a Boon
Watch the passengers — five strangers rolled on a D66 table, and the GM was pleased with the results
Finish Kostas’s recovery — daily medical care until STR/DEX/END are back to 7/10/7
Cassius’s training, eight weeks of it; StClair’s research
Read the rest of the disks — only the Boughene material and Vlen’s reminder have been described so far
Decide what the ship does about Boughene — Vlen’s intended scan target — and about Juni on Beck’s World
Still open, further away now: Harlen, Exceedingly Discreet, Darrian Jak in prison, Detective Odoy, The Device, Vlen’s body

session-2026-09-20.title: Session 2026-09-20
session-2026-09-20.content:
traveller sota session
Secrets of the Ancients
Session date: 2026-09-20
In-fiction date: roughly 212–218-1105 — mid-way through the third jump, Whanga → Alell (approximate; the table didn’t track days, only jumps)
GM’s framing: the three-week transit to Alell, one random event per jump — the three D100s rolled last session paid out one at a time. StClair’s player was absent, but the GM let the crew “use him once” (he was used three times). Ozy’s player joined from a car for the first half.
Starting position
Two or three days into the first jump, Regina → Forboldn, with five high passengers aboard and Talia asking for help with the Helix / Black Horizon row over a joint discovery. Kostas in the medbay recovering from surgery.
Live notes

Training. Eight weeks per skill; three jumps to Alell means three weeks banked if nothing interrupts. Cassius settled on Investigate after wavering towards Persuade. Ozy took Persuade — “more within the line of my character”. The GM barred Kostas from training in week one — “not while recovering in the medbay” — Kostas is training Streetwise. Using a skill at the table still doesn’t count
The Helix / Black Horizon dispute. Helix’s equipment and Black Horizon’s research both went into a breakthrough; each claims it. Not yet disturbing the passengers, “but it will eventually”. Talia at her wits’ end

Ozy read the contracts. Helix: genuinely honest, painfully bureaucratic, red tape everywhere; their terms give the ship a 2% royalty capped at Cr1,000,000. Black Horizon: secretive, encrypt everything, claim exclusive patent rights on any breakthrough and pay no royalties — and that’s in the contract the crew signed
Ozy’s carrier-clause idea from last session was a bluff (“I’m just saying, if I kept notes”). Cassius tried “this is above your pay grade, refer it to head office” — the reps are empowered to settle everything for their teams and threw that out. They wanted it sorted then and there
The plan became turn a qualitative argument into a quantitative one: pull the logs and data packets and work out each side’s percentage contribution. The GM asked whether they’d fake the numbers; Kostas (delirious in the medbay, and the only one with the spreadsheet) said don’t, the ship needs the research income. Ozy considered keeping a personal backup of the data; Black Horizon’s encryption would have raised the difficulty, so he dropped it. Difficulty stayed at 8
Ozy, Electronics (Computers) +7, rolled 5 → 12, Effect +4. The GM let him choose the outcome. He chose Black Horizon in the right — “if Black Horizon are the more dodgy, it’s easier if they’re in the right, because it’s easier to convince Helix to back down”. The records show the discovery was Black Horizon’s, “pretty much bang on”
Result: Black Horizon keep the discovery, exclusive patent, no royalties to anyone. Helix are pissed off but bound by the contract. Talia is happy — it’s off her plate. And Khei, Black Horizon’s rep, is very happy with Ozy: she thinks he looks like one of her exes


Ozy and Kay. Ozy spent part of the week chatting Kay up — “a very boring corporate-to-corporate argument for getting laid”, PowerPoint implied. The GM ruled it costs him a couple of days of training for the week. The roll succeeded; the scene went to fade to black and “went down well”. The GM promised an animation
Kostas’s recovery. Five days of care needed; by the end of the first jump he had a day or two spare. Coffees resumed
Arrival at Forboldn. Uneventful. Skimmed the gas giant — jump-2 means refuelling every leg
Jump 2, Forboldn → Whanga (two parsecs). Cassius ran the ship computer: first astrogation attempt was rolled at the wrong difficulty on Roll20 and redone — Effect +1 either way; jump drive roll +7. One week. Nobody remarked that Kostas, the ship’s astrogator, wasn’t there
Event: the smell. A few days in, a smell spread through the ship — different for everyone, always the best smell of your childhood: burning rubber, candy floss, fresh-cut grass. It didn’t fade. Everything, food and drink included, tasted of it. Both research companies: “not us”. Left alone it would have imposed Bane dice on everything done aboard

Kostas reconned the ventilation and found nothing
StClair, dragged from his lab “hair even crazier than normal, I can’t work like this”, flew a repair drone through the vents on Remote Ops (11, Effect +3) and found a blob of pulsating goo in the ducts, growing. A Medic check: it’s emitting a pheromone that overrides the sense of smell. “You’re all breathing in alien blob jizz”
The GM prompted a headcount of the passengers. Talia (Steward +3, rolled 8) went round the staterooms: one passed out drunk; one quietly keeping to their room since Regina; one rich noble twat haunting the ship like he owns it; one overly friendly, chatting to everyone and “seeing how things work”. The fifth door: a scream, and on the floor an empty skin suit
“How could it possibly be one of our passengers? We checked them so carefully”
Ozy rigged a sensor on Computers (“I’m basically trying to invent the scanner in Alien” — it goes beep): the goo’s DNA matches the inside of the skin suit. One of the five high passengers is the blob. The GM: this is what the D66 table rolled for the passengers — “it’s funny because one of them turned out to be an alien”
Killing it would forfeit its Cr60,000 passage. StClair on Science (his only science is Psionicology; a plain Science check, 9, Effect +1): the voyage coincided with the alien’s reproductive cycle and the pheromone is a mating call. It would last a few more days. Options: shut off ventilation around it or wait it out
The crew sealed the ventilation around it, no roll needed. Back in its skin suit it was sheepish, apologised (“won’t happen again” — it can talk in the suit, nobody knows how) and hid in its stateroom for the rest of the trip. No lasting effects; “everyone’s horny”


Arrival at Whanga. Skimmed the gas giant. Two weeks of training banked for Cassius and Ozy; Kostas’s first week (he’s a week behind). Kostas is back to full and out of the medbay
Jump 3, Whanga → Alell (one parsec). Cassius: astrogation Effect +2. Same jump duration as always
Event: containment breach. Peaceful, eventless — until alarms rang through the ship and a Black Horizon security detail turned up on the bridge. Specimens they’d brought aboard — under the contract clause that says the crew don’t get to look at what they bring — have escaped into the maintenance shafts. “They’re not tribbles this time.” Kostas: our maintenance shafts seem to be exposed to everything

The specimens are juvenile carthuses: tall, pale cave-dwellers from deep desert, four limbs, a spine so flexible they dislocate joints at will and worm through cracks; hide in the dark and hunt from it; normally suck the moisture out of fungus and moss, “but obviously it’s found different prey on this ship”. Three, maybe four, possibly more — Black Horizon’s count was vague (“a very slapdash operation”). Acid for blood was asked as a joke and got a “yeah” — treat as a joke
Black Horizon want them back alive, and “appreciate” means money. Stun them. The crew own no stunners; the Black Horizon security officer with them has one, StClair has a stun stick, Ozy has explosives (please not in the vents). Gunnerson is manning the guns
Marching order into the vents: security officer (stunner first), Ozy (“corporate bother boy, expendable, like in Aliens”), Kostas, Cassius at the rear. Glow sticks out; the GM’s lighting shows only the area around them
The first one came from behind, at Cassius. Initiative. Ozy shot it first — no armour, big damage, and the GM warned that another hit like that would kill it. It leapt on Cassius (attack 11, hit; bite through his Protection 10 armour for 3 END). Cassius looked for a reaction — dodge (DEX DM 0, Athletics 0), parry (Melee 1, total 1), his thruster pack — and the GM ruled nothing applied; movement isn’t a reaction. Cassius held, the security officer squeezed past and missed with the stunner. Kostas’s turn: “it looks like it’s on the verge of death, and so am I, and that fucking idiot’s just missed it. Shoot the fucker” — instead Kostas took StClair’s stun stick (2D6−1, no modifier), got in front of the Admiral and stunned it in one. “You have a snoozing alien in front of you.” The security officer was impressed: “more of that would be appreciated”
Black Horizon are sending a team to collect it. New marching order: Kostas at the rear. The GM needs to work out where the rest are — paused here, mid-hunt, one down



Decisions and discoveries

The Helix / Black Horizon row is settled in Black Horizon’s favour on Ozy’s Effect +4 Computers roll — his choice, made because a dodgy company in the right is easier to enforce than an honest one in the wrong. Black Horizon: exclusive patent, no royalties. Helix: bound, and sour. The crew gain nothing from the discovery; what it actually is was never asked
The two charter contracts are now known: Helix pays the ship a 2% royalty capped at Cr1,000,000 on breakthroughs; Black Horizon pays no royalties and claims exclusive patents; and Black Horizon’s contract forbids the crew inspecting their cargo — which is how live specimens came aboard unseen
Khei is Black Horizon’s rep aboard, and Ozy is involved with her. The Helix rep’s name was heard as “Rock Anlo” — spelling unconfirmed, no note yet
One of the five high passengers is a shapeshifting alien — a blob in a skin suit, of a species nobody named, in its mating season. Harmless, apologetic, still paying. The Five High Passengers are now mostly characterised: the drunk, the recluse, the noble, the friendly one, and the blob
Black Horizon brought live carthuses aboard and lost them into the shafts during the third jump. One stunned, two or three or more loose. Cassius bitten for 3 END
Training: Cassius Investigate, Ozy Persuade — two weeks each by Whanga (Ozy’s flirting may have cost him days of week one; the GM counted two anyway). Kostas Streetwise, one week
Rules settled: no training while in the medbay; movement/pressing a button isn’t a reaction; dodge uses DEX DM or Athletics, parry uses Melee, neither reduces damage — they penalise the attack roll; the security officer counts as a stat-block NPC the GM rolled up on the spot (Protection 6)

End position

In the third jump, Whanga → Alell, days from arrival, in the maintenance shafts hunting escaped carthuses with a Black Horizon security officer and one stun stick between them. One stunned and awaiting collection; the rest loose and roused
Cassius at END −3 from the bite. Kostas fully recovered from surgery, carrying StClair’s stun stick, at the rear
Marching order: security officer, Ozy, Cassius, Kostas
Cr300,000 in passage fees still due on arrival — all five passengers alive, one of them a blob
Helix nursing a grievance; Black Horizon in the crew’s debt twice over (the ruling, and the specimen)
Harlen, Exceedingly Discreet, Detective Odoy, Vlen’s body, Boughene, Juni on Beck’s World — all untouched this session

Priorities for next session

Finish the carthus hunt — stun, don’t kill; count them properly; nobody go alone
Land at Alell: collect Cr300,000, pay the month, and start on Vlen’s family and his burial
Ask Black Horizon what else is in their cargo — the contract says the crew can’t look, but two incidents in three weeks is grounds for a conversation
What was the discovery? Nobody asked. And what Black Horizon “appreciate” translates to in credits
Cassius’s END, StClair’s stun stick back, and buying stunners at the first port that sells them
Third week of training if the hunt doesn’t eat it
Still open, further away now: Harlen, Exceedingly Discreet, Darrian Jak in prison, Detective Odoy, The Device, Vlen’s body, Boughene, Juni

session-2026-09-27.title: Session 2026-09-27
session-2026-09-27.content:
traveller sota session
Secrets of the Ancients
Session date: 2026-09-27
In-fiction date: roughly 215–219-1105. The rest of the third jump, Whanga → Alell, then arrival at Alell (approximate; the table still counts jumps, not days)
Written from the session recording, which starts a few minutes in, partway through the second carthus fight. The table said nothing critical happened before that. Started late and paused at 11:30pm. StClair’s player was absent again, and StClair was used as an NPC twice.
Starting position
In the maintenance shafts of the Event Horizon hunting Black Horizon’s escaped carthuses with a Black Horizon security officer. One already stunned. Cassius down 3 END. Kostas fully recovered and carrying StClair’s stun stick.
Live notes

Second carthus (the recording picks up here). Kostas spotted it and aimed. Someone’s shot (12) “ripped into it”, and the GM said one more hit might kill it. The security officer has a stunner and the crew don’t. It lunged at Kostas’s “nicely new, healed face” for 16 damage, and Kostas dodged at −1 to his next round. The security officer missed with the stunner. Cassius then gave up on taking it alive: “this thing nearly took Kostas’s head off”. He aimed with his gyro-stabilised machine gun and laser sight and shredded it. The guard: “no, we need to keep them alive”
Ozy worked the guard for information with Persuade, which he’s training but can’t use yet. The GM turned down his pitch that it should count as on-the-job training. The guard said it was “above my pay grade”, and when asked how many more there were: “a handful”
Ship systems failing. A crew message reported spreading system failures near the control room. The guard’s access didn’t open the door. Kostas opened it (“in TCM we don’t just open doors, we have a conversation about it for 25 minutes”) and found two carthuses tearing into the ship’s systems, fires starting, electrical shorts

Ozy moved in first and hit hard with his laser pistol (3D6+3). One carthus went for someone, possibly Ozy, with a bite that would have done 10, and they dodged it. The security guard stunned one: “Damn. Good shot”. The table named him Pedro (“Pedro to Ops”). Kostas aimed and finished the other, not caring if it died: “Teamwork, Admiral”
Cascading failure. The GM wanted Mechanic, sensor or Computers checks. Ozy found the power cables about to overload and fixed them. Kostas had been hitting pipes with a wrench to no effect. The GM had them roll anyway: an 8 would have meant critical damage to the manoeuvre drive, −1 to all spacecraft control checks. Seven minutes to fix


Third fight, in the corridor. Pedro had gone on ahead, and the crew heard him scream: “found another one!” Kostas swapped his wrench for his gun. Pedro’s stun missed, and the carthus bit a huge chunk out of his shoulder for 13. He was bleeding badly. Cassius hit it and just missed Pedro. Then Kostas fired without aiming and blew it apart, which covered Pedro’s shoulder in bits of alien

Noises echoed around the vents. Pedro tried to patch himself up but his hands slipped in the blood. Another one attacked him and he dived prone, “crying for his mummy”. Kostas aimed and shot it (“splats against the wall”)
Another came round the corner. Cassius had held an action for exactly this and missed. It leapt on Kostas’s back with a boon die. Kostas dodged and Cassius used a leadership action to help, but it still did 19, 14 after armour 5. Kostas: END 0, STR 0, DEX 10, unconscious. The GM: “I just healed you up”. Ozy aimed and missed, and a stun attempt missed too. Pedro stunned it
Pedro called it in. StClair “appeared out of the shadows” and used the medikit Kostas was still carrying on him: rolled 8, “we’ll say it’s one”. Kostas was conscious but “not looking good”, and straight back to the medbay. The table’s running joke: “Kostas is unconscious every time we fight anyone”. “Memorial Medbay”, not yet


Clean-up. A Black Horizon xenobiologist arrived with officers to deal with “the fallen specimens” and put the stunned ones into secure containment. They were all tight-lipped about it (Per the GM in Session 2026-10-04, Black Horizon then incinerated the stunned ones as too dangerous.)
Ozy and Khei, a skill chain. First roll, Carousing: how good he was in bed. It succeeded, which gave DM+3 on the real roll, Advocate: Effect +7. What Kay told him:

Black Horizon were carrying cryogenically frozen embryos of these creatures and, separately, a growth serum. “Somehow the two of them met”: the embryos grew instantly, broke containment and got into the vents. That’s why the carthuses were weaker than adults: juveniles, freshly born
All the embryo samples have been destroyed. The growth formula has been kept
If the crew keep this quiet, the growth serum might be made available to them, if it would be useful. See Black Horizon’s Growth Serum
Ozy nudged, winked and looked under the sheets: “growth hormone, eh?” She kicked him out of the room


Kostas’s surgery. StClair operated with medbay DM+1, plus a boon die because he’s just done this operation on Kostas, “well acquainted with Kostas’s general biology”. Effect +3, END +3, then daily recovery. The GM: “you’ll be fine by the time you come out of jump, because I really don’t want you knackered”. Coming round, Kostas asked if the Admiral was all right. StClair: someone has got him a coffee, “but they can’t make it the same way you do”
Ozy went to pass on his condolences to Cassius for the substandard coffee, still naked. Cassius: “Kostas, get this pervert out of my sight”, then realised Kostas wasn’t there. Kostas, in the medbay, pulled the emergency cord because he felt the Admiral needed something
Arrival at Alell. Last of the three jumps. Alell has no gas giant and no highport, and the ship has one jump of fuel. The options raised: jump back to Whanga once business is done, or shuttle fuel up with the Implacable and pay for it. Left for later
“This is Alell patrol ship Delta 2. Prepare for inspection. Please confirm.” It showed at very long range and closed. The GM noted a lot of radiation from the system’s sun, which interfered with the first scan

Kostas ran a sensor check: good, but very long range makes it hard. Ozy assisted on Computers with a roll the GM called “cheating”: Alell doesn’t normally have patrol ships assigned
Ozy warned Black Horizon of “potential incoming authorities” (Kay gave him a pat on the bum), then Helix, who started preparing their documentation, “of which there is a lot”
Ozy asked Delta 2 for its security handshake, claiming sensor faults, and followed up by asking for the proper ship-to-ship protocol. A “wide boy” check (any skill) succeeded: they cut comms and armoured up. The table treated it as a false flag


Space combat, the first the table has fought. The GM explained it: move, attack and action phases each turn, plus reactions. Every crew member takes a role. (Sin joked that you’d get killed again; hits on the ship wounding crew is not a rule the GM stated)

The Event Horizon has three turrets: missile, pulse and beam, the pulse medium range and the beam long range. At very long range only missiles work, and they take four rounds to arrive. One rack of 12 missiles, all they have; restocking costs a quarter of a million. Each missile that gets through does 4D6 (heard as “46”), multiplied by the number still in flight. Sensors can knock incoming missiles down and give gunners locks. Improved sensors aboard
Thrust 2, which the GM called “shit thrust”. Delta 2 is faster. Nobody has shields out here, only armour. The Implacable has one fixed beam laser, usable only at dogfighting range. Flying it would split the crew, “a really good way of someone dying”, so everyone stayed aboard
Crew positions: Cassius captaining and piloting. Gunner Gunnerson on one laser turret and Kostas on the other. Atticus Brown, “the Greenhorn”, Gunner 2, on the missiles. Ozy on computers and sensors. No dedicated mechanic or engineer, so crew will swap roles if the ship takes damage. Kostas also built Cassius a coffee-loading station “like a Lancaster bomber”
Alell has no help to offer. There’s no highport and no station to call. There’s a cargo handling station in orbit, a medical facility, and a rapid-response emergency service for rescuing people lost in the jungle, but none of them take visiting ships. It’s a toxic, poisonous jungle world, used for hunting in the past, with very old First Imperium buildings. There is a starport on the surface that the Implacable can reach and the lab ship can’t. “Looks like you’re going to be on your own out here”
Initiative: 2D6 + Pilot (Cassius, 2) + Thrust (2), plus Cassius’s Tactics (Naval). The first roll was the wrong skill, at −4 (“you’re all flustered, Admiral”). It ended around 7, and the numbers in the recording don’t fully add up. Delta 2 came straight at them
Manoeuvre: run parallel/across its course and let it close. Six turns to short range, about four until it’s in pulse range
Decision to fire. It’s broadcasting under a false flag, it cut comms and armoured up: “I don’t think they’re coming to deliver some fresh coffee beans”. Turn 1: the Greenhorn launched three missiles, leaving 9
Ozy tried to identify the ship and its capabilities from sensor data. It’s too far to tell, but he picked up missile heat signatures, more than one, incoming (Rich asked for this to be scratched in Session 2026-10-04. Delta 2’s first salvo was the one Kostas detected in round 1 there.)
Paused here, turn 1, missiles in flight both ways. The GM will roll up Delta 2’s crew before next session



Decisions and discoveries

The carthus hunt is over. Four killed (one by Cassius’s machine gun, three by Kostas) and two stunned (both by Pedro). With last session’s that’s seven, three taken alive. Black Horizon wanted them all alive
What the carthuses were: frozen embryos that hit Black Horizon’s growth serum by accident and matured on the spot. The embryos are destroyed. Black Horizon kept the serum and is offering it to the crew for their silence. Nobody has answered yet
Ship damage from the carthuses was fixed by Ozy before it went critical
Kostas down again: END 0 / STR 0 at the time, then patched, operated on (Effect +3) and fit again by the end of the jump, per the GM
Pedro, Black Horizon’s security guard, lost a large piece of his shoulder
Delta 2 is claiming to be an Alell patrol ship. Alell doesn’t normally have patrol ships. It went silent when asked to authenticate, armoured up, closed at speed and has fired missiles. Who it really is is unknown
Alell system facts: no gas giant, no highport, heavy solar radiation, orbital cargo station, surface starport the lab ship can’t use. Fuel is now a problem: one jump left in the tanks
Rules settled: reactions (dodge) apply against the next round’s actions, and you can wait to see whether the attack hits before dodging. Armour comes off after the dodge. Damage takes END first, then STR or DEX, and two characteristics at 0 means unconscious. Space combat runs by range bands: missiles only at very long, four rounds of travel, 4D6 per missile. Initiative is 2D6 + Pilot + Thrust + Tactics (Naval). The GM’s Space Combat Cheat Sheet has the sensor-range table

End position

Alell system, turn 1 of a space fight with Delta 2: very long range, closing, missiles in flight both ways (three of theirs out, an unknown number of the enemy’s incoming)
Crew at stations: Cassius piloting, Gunnerson and Kostas on the laser turrets, Atticus on missiles, Ozy on sensors. Nobody on damage control
Missiles: 9 of 12 left. Restock Cr250,000
Fuel: one jump. No gas giant here
Kostas fit again, per the GM. Cassius was still down 3 END from last session, and nothing was said about healing it
Pedro badly injured. Carthus hunt finished, three specimens in containment. Black Horizon’s serum offer on the table
Cr300,000 in passage fees due on arrival and not yet collected: they haven’t made orbit
Harlen, Exceedingly Discreet, Detective Odoy, Vlen’s body, Boughene, Juni on Beck’s World: all untouched this session

Priorities for next session

Survive Delta 2. Missile defence on sensors, keep out of its better ranges, work out who it really is. Ask whether “Alell patrol” is a cover for pirates, someone after Black Horizon’s cargo, or someone after the crew
Put someone on damage control. There’s no mechanic aboard, so decide in advance who swaps off a station
Answer Kay about the growth serum: take it, refuse it, or ask what it actually does
Fuel: shuttle it up with the Implacable, or jump back to Whanga after
Once down: collect the Cr300,000, pay the month, and start on Vlen’s family and his burial
Black Horizon’s “appreciation” for the hunt is still unpaid. Buy stunners at the first port that sells them
Still open, further away now: Harlen, Exceedingly Discreet, Darrian Jak in prison, Detective Odoy, The Device, Vlen’s body, Boughene, Juni

session-2026-10-04.title: Session 2026-10-04
session-2026-10-04.content:
traveller sota session
Secrets of the Ancients
Session date: 2026-10-04
In-fiction date: c. 219-1105, arrival at Alell
Written from the live notes taken during play, checked against the session recording (OBS, 21:26–23:21). The table’s first space combat, learned as they went: most of the session is the fight with Delta 2. StClair’s player was absent again; the GM offered StClair as an NPC for comms or repairs (he has Computers and Remote Ops, no Electronics (sensors)). Round numbers below are the GM’s.
Starting position

Turn 1 of a space fight with Delta 2 in the Alell system: very long range, closing. Three of the Event Horizon’s missiles in flight. Delta 2 claims to be an Alell patrol ship, but Alell has none, and it went dark when asked to authenticate
Stations: Cassius piloting, Gunner Gunnerson and Kostas on the laser turrets, Atticus Brown on missiles, Ozy on sensors. Nobody on damage control
Missiles 9 of 12 (restock Cr250,000). Fuel: one jump, no gas giant. Thrust 2; Delta 2 is faster
Kostas fit again; Cassius possibly still down 3 END
Black Horizon’s growth serum offer for silence unanswered (Black Horizon’s Growth Serum). Cr300,000 passage fees not yet collected

Live notes
Round 1 (continued from last session, the round the first salvo went out)

The GM ran through the round: manoeuvre, attack, actions, with reactions in between. Captains can improve initiative with Leadership; engineers repair or overload; sensors can detect launches, lock, jam comms and knock out missiles
Station swap. Ozy has good Electronics but not Electronics (sensors), so he can’t do electronic warfare; Kostas (Electronics (sensors) 1) is the only one aboard who can. Kostas moved to sensors and Ozy to engineering. The GM allowed the swap for free because the table had muddled who had which skills. Kostas’s laser turret was left unmanned
Cassius: Leadership for initiative, “not the best”
Kostas: the GM allowed a sensor check to detect launches: rolled 8, detected a missile launch, number unknown. (Last session’s turn-1 report of Delta 2 missiles is folded into this; Rich asked for it to be scratched as a separate sighting.)
Ozy: asked whether anything could cut the time or difficulty of an emergency jump. Jumping in combat raises the difficulty a step, and needs Engineer (j-drive). Checked the Event Horizon’s quirks (she’s second-hand): nothing combat-related, just −10 Hull
Ozy then rolled an overload of the manoeuvre drive (Engineer +4, a 10+ check) and the GM granted three Thrust for next round, then read on: every repeat takes a cumulative DM−2. The table held the overload in reserve for when it would matter. (The recording doesn’t make clear whether the roll stood; the GM later treated round 4’s overload as the first.)
Delta 2 thrusting flat out towards the Event Horizon. Missile flight time is fixed by the range at launch: movement doesn’t change it
Airlocks, for a boarding party: one under the air/raft, one at the end of the docking ring where the Implacable connects, and an unspecified number around the circular section. Kostas floated stocking them with carthuses. The GM said Black Horizon had incinerated the stunned carthuses, judging them too dangerous

Round 2

Manoeuvre: Cassius cut thrust and held station. The GM: no momentum, “Star Wars, Battlestar Galactica physics” — cut thrust and you stop
Attack: Atticus launched another 3 missiles. 6 of 12 left. The table squabbled over the cost; the Admiral, “captain and lord, your master and your God”, wants missiles every round
Cassius: Leadership, Effect +8
Kostas: Electronic Warfare against the incoming salvo, a Difficult (10+) check: rolled 6, failed
Ozy: nothing to do; texting

Round 3 — the Event Horizon’s Initiative 15 beat Delta 2’s 12

Still at very long range, because the Event Horizon isn’t moving towards Delta 2
Attack: Atticus launched another 3 missiles. 3 of 12 left
Cassius: Leadership, Effect +4
Kostas: Electronic Warfare, Effect 0: no missiles removed, but he detected that Delta 2 had launched a second salvo. (The GM explained after the fight that this launch was the round before, not this round.)
The GM moved Delta 2 one hex closer. He checked a ruling here

Round 4 — Delta 2 rolled badly but still went first

Gunnerson is on the pulse laser. The beam laser is unmanned
Ozy: overloaded the manoeuvre drive, rolled 12: Thrust 3 for round 5. The next overload would need 12+
Kostas: Electronic Warfare on the first incoming salvo, failed
Cassius: Leadership, failed (“Yay, I knew it”)
No missiles launched this round

Round 5 — within long range now; Delta 2 went first

Delta 2’s first salvo arrived. At this range the crew could see it: four missiles. Cassius spent a Thrust on Evasive Action (DM−2). Gunnerson tried point defence with the pulse laser (Gunner +2): missed. Atticus had meant to move to the beam laser, but nobody had said so, so it stayed empty
The salvo rolled 10 (with +4 for missiles, −2 evasion): Effect +2. The Event Horizon has no armour, so nothing came off: 4D6 × 2 = 20 damage. The GM briefly read it as ×4
Starting Hull 124. 20 damage crossed a 10% threshold: a Severity 1 critical to the Hull, 1D extra damage: 3. Hull 101. “You can hear systems start alerting, but it’s holding together”
Manoeuvre: Cassius put 2 Thrust towards Delta 2. Still long range
Attack: Atticus fired the last 3 missiles. Missiles 0 of 12. Firing used his turn, so he couldn’t change turrets
The Event Horizon’s first salvo hit: Delta 2’s defences destroyed one of its three missiles, leaving +2; Effect +2, 30 damage. The GM rolled two lots of 2D6 afterwards (12 and 8), outcome not stated
Kostas: Sensor Lock (contested, helps turret fire, not missiles): failed. Ozy: nothing he could fix (Hull damage can’t be quick-repaired)
Cassius: Leadership, Effect +5

Round 6 — the Event Horizon at 12, Delta 2 at −4: the Event Horizon went first

Cassius held station: no movement
Two of the Event Horizon’s salvos reached Delta 2, three missiles each, rolled separately at +3. The first: Effect +3, 28 damage (58 in total). The GM rolled seven lots of 2D6 for the damage chain. Delta 2 exploded: secondary explosions ripped through it, then the second salvo “obliterates the hulk”, fuel lines and gas venting on fire. Delta 2 destroyed
But two Delta 2 salvos were already in flight, both launched the round before Kostas detected the second launch:

The first: Cassius evaded; point defence missed again. Roll 11, Effect +3. 18 × 3 = 54 damage. Three Severity 1 criticals (2D6 rolls of 3, 12 and 10): Power Plant (Power −10%), Bridge (a random station disabled: the GM made it comms), Jump Drive (DM−2 to all jump drive checks)
The second: Cassius evaded with his last Thrust. Roll 8, Effect 0: it hits, but missile damage is multiplied by the Effect, so no damage


Hull 47 of 124, “about half”. The GM: if Delta 2 had gone first it would have been in range with its beam laser and could have shot down some of the crew’s missiles: “good captaining there, Admiral”
A passenger in the beam laser. The GM had forgotten one of the Five High Passengers, “the friendly one” who’d asked how everything on the ship works, wanted to stay aboard and help. Retconned in: he took the beam laser for one of the salvos, untrained (DM−3), and destroyed no missiles. He’ll still pay his fare. The GM offered him as an extra crew member, to be rolled up; the table seemed keen
Aftermath. Ozy rolled Engineer and fixed the comms. Sensors clear: nothing else out there. First space combat won, without ever getting into laser range

Who Delta 2 was (GM, after the fight): a Far Trader with two weapons, a missile rack and a beam laser. One more hex and it could have shot at the Event Horizon or at her missiles. The table had guessed “space pirate”. During the fight the GM framed it as preying on a lab ship it thought was easy pickings and probably unarmed. Nobody aboard has been identified.
After the fight

The Event Horizon has another hard point free for a turret (a sandcaster was mentioned), and upgrades can be bought when there’s money
The passengers. Talia tried to calm them (+3, rolled 9, Effect +1) and Ozy followed up with Advocate (+1 from Talia): it went fine. (Ozy joked that a couple of them were paying extra for the excitement; they weren’t.) The story for outsiders: not a pirate attack but a successful elimination of a threat in the system, with the passengers part of it
Into orbit. The Event Horizon is parked in orbit in Alell’s shadow, out of the radiation. The Implacable takes the passengers down: Cr300,000 in fares collected
The monthly bill (mortgage, maintenance) is due now
The ship is badly hurt and Alell can’t fix her: no highport, no starport in orbit, and nobody aboard has the skills for Hull repairs. Whoever stays up to repair her is out of whatever happens on the surface. Power −10% doesn’t affect them in practice; jump checks DM−2; comms fixed; Hull about half; fuel for one parsec, no gas giant
The GM read the chapter’s arrival blurb (paraphrased): the lonely run along the Spinward Main, systems without starports, refuelling from gas giants or automated hydrogen harvesters; Alell circles an angry, energetic star, and from orbit the jungles show gold and red, with the lights of walled resorts here and there. (The blurb assumes a corpse in the hold. Corrected 2026-10-18: so does this game, the body came with them.)
Training: three jumps is three weeks. Cassius gets three weeks. Ozy gets none, having been otherwise occupied (the table’s joke). A skill point takes eight weeks of training and then an EDU check. The GM: progression in this game is mostly buying better gear, weapons and cyber implants
Chapter 2 preview: less investigation, a little, and a lot of NPCs. Some of them are Kostas’s family: Alell is where Kostas was born.

Decisions and discoveries

Delta 2 destroyed in round 6: a Far Trader (missile rack, beam laser) posing as an Alell patrol ship. 58 damage from the Event Horizon’s missiles, then the hulk obliterated. Who was aboard, and why, is unknown
All 12 missiles spent. Restock Cr250,000
The Event Horizon took 77 damage: Hull 47 of 124. She has no armour (the GM confirmed). Criticals: Hull (1D, done), Power Plant (Power −10%), Bridge comms (fixed by Ozy), Jump Drive (DM−2 to jump checks, still broken)
Cr300,000 in fares collected
The friendly passenger helped in the beam laser and may join the crew, to be rolled up
Black Horizon incinerated the stunned carthuses, per the GM: none were kept alive after all
Alell is Kostas’s birthplace, and some of chapter 2’s NPCs are his family
Rules settled at the table: missile flight time depends only on range at launch, not on movement afterwards. Electronic Warfare against missiles is Difficult (10+) Electronics (sensors). Sensor Lock is contested and helps turret fire, not missiles. Evasive Action works against missiles, using unspent Thrust. Each salvo attacks separately, +1 per missile. Missile damage is multiplied by the attack’s Effect, so Effect 0 does no damage. Every 10% of starting Hull lost is a Severity 1 critical. Overloading the drive again takes a cumulative DM−2. Hull damage can’t be quick-repaired in combat. No momentum: cutting thrust stops the ship

End position

Event Horizon in orbit over Alell, in the planet’s shadow. Hull 47 of 124, no armour. Jump drive damaged (DM−2), power −10%, comms repaired. Missiles 0 of 12. One jump of fuel, no gas giant, no highport
Passengers delivered by the Implacable; Cr300,000 collected
Monthly mortgage and maintenance due now
The friendly passenger may be staying on as crew
Black Horizon’s growth serum offer still unanswered; their “appreciation” for the carthus hunt still unpaid
Harlen, Exceedingly Discreet, Detective Odoy, Vlen’s body, Boughene, Juni on Beck’s World: untouched

Priorities for next session

Pay the month and work out what’s left: see Ship Finances
Repairs: who stays aboard to fix the Event Horizon, and where Hull repairs can be had at all. The jump drive (DM−2) matters before any jump
Fuel: shuttle it up with the Implacable, or one jump back to Whanga
Restock missiles (Cr250,000), and consider a fourth turret on the free hard point
Roll up the friendly passenger if he’s joining the crew
Alell: Kostas’s family, Vlen’s family and his burial
Answer Khei about the growth serum; chase Black Horizon’s “appreciation”
Still open: Harlen, Exceedingly Discreet, Darrian Jak in prison, Detective Odoy, The Device, Vlen’s body, Boughene, Juni

session-2026-10-18.title: Session 2026-10-18
session-2026-10-18.content:
traveller sota session
Secrets of the Ancients
Session date: 2026-10-18
In-fiction date: the day the crew went down to Alell, shortly after c. 219-1105 (not stated). Midday at the homecoming
Written from the session recording (OBS, 21:14–23:02), transcribed with Whisper. Names are checked against the GM’s handouts and image filenames where possible; anything Whisper may have mangled is marked. All four players present, StClair’s player back after missing two sessions. Chapter 2 opens: almost no combat, a lot of NPCs, and a family funeral that turns into a fight over Vlen’s estate.
Starting position

Event Horizon in orbit over Alell, in the planet’s shadow. Hull 47 of 124, jump drive damaged (DM−2), missiles 0 of 12, one jump of fuel
Passengers delivered by the Implacable; Cr300,000 collected. The month’s mortgage and maintenance due
Vlen Backett’s body aboard in a cryotube, for burial on Alell
The friendly passenger may be joining the crew

Live notes
Aboard ship

The friendly passenger joins the crew. He wanted in, and while StClair was away “everyone said yes”. The GM rolled him up from the Quick Characters tables (Core Rulebook p. 92): Experienced Combatant, +2 on gun skills, +1 piloting small craft (not the lab ship). Quirk: the GM first read “in debt to criminals”, then corrected it to “has secret allies”. The GM said the quirk was out-of-game knowledge, and that he doesn’t have time to build the subplot in yet. Name rolled from tables: Zed Cole (heard on the recording as “Zed Cole”). See Zed Cole
Pay banter: the Admiral proposed a six-year “trial period” without pay, to keep the ship’s cash troubles quiet. The table ended on “he gets a salary”. Amount not set
StClair caught up on the ship damage. The crew all blame the Admiral; he says he saved them. StClair wants to dock his pay over the damage and the spent missiles
Recap for StClair: Khei (Black Horizon’s cat-woman rep, “well in there” with Ozy) and Rok (Helix’s hyena-man rep) fought over the joint discovery, Talia was overworked, the carthuses got loose, and Black Horizon’s Growth Serum might come in useful
Missiles: the table agreed to buy more eventually, and not let the Admiral fire them

Down to the starport

The GM read the chapter’s arrival text: the lonely run along the Spinward Main, Alell’s angry star, gold and red jungles, the walled resorts. It mentions “the corpse in the cargo hold”
The Implacable flew down to the Alell Starport and into the mouth of the pyramid: a gigantic artificial cavern, more temple than landing site, big enough to swallow a warship. The pinnace was sprayed with jets of chemical disinfectant under strong UV lights: biological control
There’s a cargo handling station in orbit, but nothing that can help the Event Horizon
Customs (GM, through Kostas as the local expert):

Blades allowed, because people need them to get through the jungle. Armour and vacc suits fine. Guns banned; firearms stay aboard the Implacable, which is safe to leave there
Absolutely no importing anything. Taking anything out is “somewhat frowned upon”. “Everything here is pretty much trying to kill you”
Protective suits for visitors not in vacc suits. The atmosphere is fine, but the plant life gives off a toxic gas that affects anyone not acclimatised. Kostas was asked whether he’s acclimatised; the player went without a suit (“raw dog”) and plans to buy a vacc suit while here
Misters: hand sprayers of fauna and flora repellent, issued free to visitors. The mist damages skin, hence the suits
Vlen’s cryotube had to go through customs to be scanned and disinfected


Kit: Kostas, a cutlass on his hip. StClair, a bright pink hazmat suit, a little dagger and his stealth dagger. The Admiral, a cutlass (“always”). Ozy, his fists (“Mr Lefty and Mr Righty”). Kostas produced a stun stick and lent it to Ozy. It’s the one borrowed from StClair, though Kostas claimed he “found it lying around”
The customs scanner glitched on Vlen’s cryotube. Screens glitched and there were confused faces. They ran it back through and it passed, put down to “some weird glitch in the system”

The flight to Vaca Goya

Air shuttles wait outside the starport with pilots, like taxis. One was big enough for the party and the cryotube. Shuttles carry misters too, which keep the fauna and flora off in flight
The pilot: Rao, name read off the window, pronounced “Rayo”. She knew the Backett resemblance, and has ferried Vlen around a few times over the years. She thought him secretive
Her spiel: before the First Imperium fell, Alell was where nobles came to hunt. Since its rediscovery it’s become a mix of science and conservation. Most settlements have high walls; some smaller ones use a sensor grid instead. Stick together, take a guide: “this place can eat you alive if you let it”
Kostas added “interesting facts” of his own. Judging by her face they were wrong, but she played along
Kostas told her he left to “secure his fortune, chase glory in the Navy”, and that it could have gone better
Rao’s story about Vlen: some while ago he chartered her to fly him out into the middle of nowhere, no questions asked. She picked him up a week later, unharmed. “You don’t go out into those jungles alone. He was mad for doing that”
Kostas paid her Cr100 to jog her memory. She dug out a moth-eaten map and marked roughly where she dropped him off, warning it was a while ago. See Rao’s Map
The Admiral told Kostas off for spending his own money with a “rich fucker” (StClair) aboard who won’t dip into his pockets. StClair: the ship goes nowhere unless he presses the button
The view: trees taller than skyscrapers, “very reminiscent of the Jurassic”, and flocks of whisperhawks with brilliant plumage around the shuttle. The aurora casts blood-red shadows
Kostas got Rao’s number for another ride

Vaca Goya

A small village on a hilltop, inside a ring of metal poles topped with motion-sensitive mist sprayers: Tel’s map’s green dots. Green is good. “If they ever go red, watch out.”
Founded on a nearby uranium deposit. The mines are largely exhausted; it’s now forestry and farming. Population about a thousand
The GM said the village map is AI-generated; there isn’t one in the book
The flyer landed on the outskirts beside four other shuttles. Kostas didn’t recognise them
Porter Sajan is the local magistrate and spiritual leader, waiting at the village hall
Kostas showed the others round: his old school, the old house. The village looks smaller than he remembers. He once jumped out of a tree there

The homecoming, at the village hall

Crowded, mostly villagers there for the free drinks, plus a few off-world visitors from the resorts in environmental suits. Nobody seems sad about Vlen: no tears, no wailing widows
Porter Sajan, tall, in ceremonial robes, with a doleful voice “as if apologising in advance”: “I presume you’ve brought the body.” Kostas introduced StClair (“very esteemed researcher”), Ozy (“high-level business executive”) and the Admiral. The Admiral announced another medal due for “blowing away pirates” and his 20% commission from the missile company
Sajan, privately to Kostas: tonight is Vlen’s homecoming. Tomorrow is the burial and the reading of the will. “You do have the will with you, don’t you?”
Kostas has no will. It was never among the effects collected on Regina. He said “Yes, definitely” first, then admitted it. Sajan had been told Vlen would have a copy with him. “There must be another copy somewhere.” He took charge of the body
Kostas’s parents are here. His mother, Henna Backett, went straight to the Admiral’s side (“so good to see you again”) and asked whether her boy’s coffee was up to standard. The Admiral said it had been poor lately; Kostas says only when he was unconscious and in surgery. “Shouldn’t have got shot then, should you, boy?” His father, Merrick Backett: “You look a mess, boy.” Sad news about Vlen, “although you won’t find any sad faces in there. We’re all waiting for that will reading.”
Kostas’s father ran down who’s here: Tomas, Hans and Nairal. Tomas’s son Gunter isn’t, “doing his own work”. The Jocells are here, and so are the Parads: “watch your step”
The Jocells. The GM showed images of Marisa and her “asshole of a son” Bard, who work in the starport area. Kostas introduced “my best friend, the Admiral”. Bard was impressed by the uniform and medals. Marisa wasn’t, though the Admiral said aloud that she’s hot. The Admiral’s SOC is 15; they were overawed and plainly trying to work out how to use it. Marisa still had a go at Kostas (“I remember when you were a snotty little boy”), then took Bard off for a drink. “But Mother, his medals!”
StClair went outside to study the flowers, sketching while snipping the ones worth stealing. Investigate, Profession and Survival rolls: he found some interesting plants. The GM will tell him privately what’s poisonous or useful. Nobody saw, because everyone was busy drinking
Ozy made a beeline for Tomas, “the head of the family”. Tomas is a local merchant; Alell’s main trade is exotic furs and unusual minerals and ores. Ozy pitched export business. Tomas: “Quite a few have arrived with claims of their own.” Someone is “over there wanting spaceships” (Marisa, it later turned out), and Yusul Parad wants a debt of a considerable amount repaid. Ozy offered his services as a neutral third party in bartering and legalese, and Tomas accepted (“my man”). Tomas then asked whether they’d brought the will; Ozy referred him to Kostas
The family tree, corrected at the table: Tomas and Hans are brothers, not cousins, and Nairal is their uncle, which makes him Kostas’s great-uncle. Kostas reckons Tomas is his uncle. Hans “looks a bit like a hunter”; Nairal looks close to death’s door
StClair came back in and told Marisa and Bard they looked very similar: were they husband and wife? Marisa blushed, said “this is my son”, and noted StClair was unattached. Then she asked his social standing. “Hermit.” SOC −4 (as said at the table). She raised a handkerchief to her mouth and called Bard away. StClair wiped a muddy hand on the bench
Yusul Parad and a bodyguard watched Kostas and the Admiral walk by, arm in arm. The table now calls the Admiral Kostas’s boyfriend
Nairal greeted Kostas: “Is that you, Kostas? Come here, boy.” He cried and hugged him. Kostas: “I’m just glad Uncle Tomas hasn’t done you in yet.” (Family joke. “He’s a dick”)
Nairal on Vlen: “I always remember being introduced to him. He was my great-uncle. Never understood it.” He didn’t look a day over 50. See Vlen Backett’s True Age
Nairal: Vlen was never around, always off-world. He had a lodge out in the woods (not a hunting lodge; those aren’t allowed now), and sometimes came back with off-world people who’d go to the lodge. The family don’t know where it is. Kostas thinks it’s where Rao marked her map, and showed the map to no one: he doesn’t trust anyone here
More shuttles landed

The claimants arrive

Aail of the Brotherhood of Humaniti came in dancing: green robes (hers very revealing), shaved heads, three monks behind her chanting a mantra while she spoke. Name heard as “Ail”/“Ayl”; the image file spells it Aail. “The initiate Zu, known to the secular world as Vlen Backett, was a member of our order some years ago. He fled our monastery in the dead of night and never returned. As part of his initiation he signed over all worldly goods to the Brotherhood of Humaniti. It has taken us some time to find Zu’s homeworld. We claim what is rightfully ours.” (Spelled Zu, per Rich.) The GM shared an AI video of the dance on Discord
The Brotherhood (GM reading): an esoteric group who believe all humanity must unite as one, and who love every human “in a distinctly uncomfortable way”: “treat every human like you want nothing more than to keep them safe forever, like a collection of butterflies”
The monks hugged everyone. Hans was mortified. StClair went in for a hug and was well received (“Blessed be the child”), then sat on a bench in a state of bliss. He realised he may have contaminated her with sap from the plants he’d been picking, and kept quiet. The Admiral was left queueing for his own hug
Then a second woman came in, shyly, after the monks had done their thing: fully grown, fully clothed, with hair, and a Southern accent. “My name is Orisa Backett. Vlen was my husband.” (Spelling per Rich.) To Kostas: “I’m your aunt. Come here, my little nephew,” with a big hug and a kiss on the cheek. She went straight to Tomas and Nairal. Tomas: “Her husband, Vlen? Rubbish.” “I tell you I am his wife. And this is my wedding certificate.” Tomas, flustered, kept glancing at Kostas
Kostas shouted to Tomas that he might want a word with the monks. Tomas: “You’re not coming back here and landing your problems on my lap. I’m not dealing with them”
Kostas paid his respects to Yusul Parad, with the Admiral. Yusul: “I hate the Backetts, but you, I know I can trust you to do the right thing. Your uncle owes me money.” How much? “Just a cool million credits.” He is restraining himself out of respect for the funeral, but if he doesn’t see his money soon there will be trouble
His muscle, Morgan, a “hunk of muscle” (no gun; they’re illegal). Yusul twice called the Admiral “lippy”: “He ought to watch himself, otherwise he might find himself in a bit of an accident”
The Admiral argued that Vlen’s debts pass with the family name to the head of the family, or to the wife nobody knew about. He doubts the wedding certificate is worth the paper, and assumes Yusul has receipts
Yusul, leaning in: “I know what your uncle was up to. I know who he was involved with. He was trading in ancient artefacts. Those things fetch quite a penny. If any of these artefacts might just fall into my possession, we’ll maybe see about getting this debt cleared.” He isn’t patient. Kostas promised to let him know first. “That’s why I like him, Morgan”
Orisa showed her wedding certificate to anyone who’d listen. The monks have paperwork showing Initiate Zu signed over all his worldly goods. Marisa Jocell: “We’re not last in line. He owes me his spaceship. I’m not losing out to these monks and this wife.” Yusul grew more riled up
Kostas’s parents and Porter Sajan came back out of the office. Sajan went round the room, but nothing he did calmed it down

Sajan hands it to Kostas

Sajan: as the person who brought the body, with friends, Kostas can act as an intermediary. He asks Kostas and the crew to resolve these claims for tomorrow, and the will. Sajan has too many duties: the Brotherhood want their own ceremony for their initiate, “some DNA thing that will take hours”. “Preposterous.” “I trust you and believe in you, Kostas.” He bowed and left without waiting for a yes
Kostas’s father: no vehicle today. “Things are getting a bit dangerous out there this time of day,” and there won’t be many shuttle pilots. “Best to do that tomorrow, boy.” His mother: don’t leave the Admiral alone, make sure he gets what he needs
The Backetts have no security: “we’re not well-to-do”. The village hall has terminals for checking the claims. Ozy wants network access to test whether they hold up
The GM’s reminder: the statuette from the redhead’s office on the base. The table wondered whether it hides a will, and the Admiral wanted to break it open. The GM confirmed it was scanned: nothing inside, not hollow
StClair, after the hug: “I have felt two things I’ve never felt before.” Euphoric, and not following any of it
Ended there, midday. Next week the GM promises the Southern drawl again

Decisions and discoveries

New crew member: Zed Cole, Experienced Combatant, small-craft pilot. Quirk: secret allies
Alell rules: blades yes, guns no, armour and vacc suits fine, nothing imported, nothing taken out. Plant gas means visitors wear suits. Misters are free
The scanner glitch on Vlen’s cryotube is noted, not explained. It may matter given The Device and the electrical interference that has followed this case (connection drawn here, not at the table)
Rao flew Vlen into the jungle and collected him a week later. Rao’s Map marks roughly where. Kostas has kept it to himself
Vlen had a lodge in the woods, location unknown to the family, visited by off-world guests. Probably the same thread as Vlen’s Hidden Fortune
Nairal, 92, was introduced to Vlen as a child as his great-uncle. Independent support for Vlen Backett’s True Age
No will. Sajan expected Kostas to bring one. The reading is tomorrow
Four claims on Vlen’s estate, plus the family’s. See Claims on Vlen’s Estate:

Brotherhood of Humaniti: he signed everything over as Initiate Zu, and has paperwork to show it
Orisa Backett: his wife, with a wedding certificate
Yusul Parad: Cr1,000,000 owed, or ancient artefacts in lieu
Marisa Jocell: “he owes me his spaceship”


Yusul says Vlen traded in ancient artefacts and that he knows who Vlen was involved with. That fits the statuette and Ujinka’s Research
Vlen was a Brotherhood initiate who fled. It’s the first direct link between Vlen and the Brotherhood, who already had an interest in Ancients sites
Family tree corrected: Tomas and Hans are brothers; Nairal is their uncle
Ozy is now Tomas’s “neutral third party” for the inheritance

solomani-hypothesis.title: Solomani Hypothesis
solomani-hypothesis.content:
traveller sota clue
Secrets of the Ancients
The theory that Humaniti originally evolved on the planet of Terra, home of the Solomani. According to it, The Ancients transplanted primitive humans to other worlds across the galaxy — most notably the homeworlds of the Vilani and the Zhodani.
Genetic evidence has largely confirmed it, though some scientists and religious groups advocate other origins for Humaniti, such as parallel evolution or divine intervention.
Why it’s in the file
Its confirmation is what gave rise to the Brotherhood of Humaniti — and the Brotherhood’s doctrine goes further, holding that the Ancients destroyed an ur-race of ‘true Humaniti’ when they split the species into tribes.
So the Ancients didn’t merely leave ruins in the Spinward Marches. They made the people currently arguing over those ruins.
