the-ancients.title: The Ancients
the-ancients.content:
traveller sota species clue
Secrets of the Ancients
Colloquial name for a species that lived 300,000 years ago. Comparatively little is known about them.
What they did

Believed responsible for transplanting Humaniti from its original homeworld of Terra (the Solomani Hypothesis) and scattering the species across hundreds of planets
Believed to have uplifted the Vargr from Terran canines
Exceedingly high technology — many artefacts are millennia beyond cutting-edge Imperial science. Estimates of high-end Ancients tech place them beyond TL25

Their sites
Several have been discovered across Charted Space, especially in the Spinward Marches — where the party currently are.

The technology at these sites varies considerably, suggesting different Ancients groups pursued radically different paths of development
Most sites show damage consistent with orbital bombardment or other violence
There are anomalies in other systems explicable only by weapons that destroyed entire planets
That, plus their sudden disappearance from known space, has produced the Ancients Extinction Theories
Ancients sites also show common use of Droyne as pets or servants

Why this matters here
Iaros Ujinka was tracing links between G-Band Transmissions and Ancients sites — see Ujinka’s Research. Vlen Backett was going to fund and crew the expedition. Both are now dead.
Threads worth holding together, none of them established:

Vlen was a man that Vargr crossed hundreds of parsecs to consult — and the Vargr are an Ancients-uplifted species
The Church of the Chosen Ones holds that Vargr are the rightful heirs of the Ancients
The Brotherhood of Humaniti holds that the Ancients broke humanity, and that institutions opposing its reunification must be destroyed
Vlen Backett’s True Age: at least 180 years old, physiologically 52, no anagathics. Nobody has explained that

At Dancado, during the attack on Iaros Ujinka, the power was cut and a security drone taken out. Electrical systems failing at the exact moment of an attack — the same signature as the interference on the hostel footage.
If that’s the same device, the same crew is running both hits, and knocking out power and security is the opening move rather than a side effect.
Kostas Backett asked Pallod Norrim about the attackers’ apparent ability to disable systems in a localised area. Pallod dismissed it, the grav car and any connection between the murders as coincidence and nothing to worry about.

The third man was carrying a device — see The Device.

Two identified at Dancado
At Dancado, two men came in through the front door and upstairs; one was killed and the other knocked unconscious and later taken into POC custody — clearly the same two men from the footage.
That confirms the two attacks are the work of the same crew. Before the authorities arrived, the surviving intruder mentioned Ven Yasha but gave little else.

Pallod Norrim later said the POC had arrested Darrian Jak for Vlen’s murder and confirmed that Jak is short and red-haired. That matches the third man’s broad description, but it is not an independent identification.

tusal.title: Tusal
tusal.content:
traveller sota item
Secrets of the Ancients
An illegal narcotic, usually sold as tablets, though some prefer it in its less processed, undried form as a wad to be chewed. Derived from a seaweed.
Origin unknown, but believed to have been imported from the Vargr extents about a century ago. Now grown on various worlds along the Corridor sector.
Effects

A dose produces mild euphoria and intoxication
A very strong dose dulls pain receptors and causes unconsciousness
Users stay functional on a low dose, so many addicts chew six or seven tablets a day to hold a constant drugged haze

Who uses it
Especially associated with menial jobs and the unemployed — an otherwise dull life of drudgery made pleasant. Long-term addiction brings respiratory and digestive problems and a high incidence of stomach cancer.
Bearing on the murder
Vlen Backett had 200 ng/mL in his blood when he died — per the coroner, enough that he would barely have been able to stand, let alone fight back. That is squarely the “very strong dose” band: pain receptors dulled, heading for unconsciousness.
Two things that don’t fit a recreational user:

The drug’s user base is menial labourers and the unemployed holding a low functional dose. Vlen was neither, and his dose was nowhere near low.
A man that sedated doesn’t wander into a very strong dose by accident and then happen to be shot through the heart at close range with no defensive wounds.

It reads as a dose given to him to make the killing easy — inference, not established. See Vlen Backett’s Murder.
Darrian Jak sold a lot of Tusal in Credo City the night Vlen died — the party’s best lead on where this batch came from.
Loose thread
Tusal is believed to have come out of the Vargr extents. Vlen was a man that Vargr crossed hundreds of parsecs to consult. Probably nothing — the drug’s been in Imperial space a century and is grown locally — but it’s noted.
Notes

ujinka's-research.title: Ujinka's Research
ujinka's-research.content:
traveller sota clue
Secrets of the Ancients
Iaros Ujinka was investigating links between G-Band Transmissions and sites of Ancient technology. That’s what took her to Beck’s World, and it is what she and Vlen Backett were going to discuss.
Vlen’s involvement
Vlen was going to provide funding and a ship to support the research. That is the “topics of mutual interest” from his letter — and it means a drifter with no visible income was in a position to bankroll a university research programme and put a hull under it.
He was murdered before the meeting happened.
The proposal to the party
Before her death, Ujinka asked whether the party could use the Event Horizon to support the research instead. No final answer given yet.
The Event Horizon is a Lab Ship. She is, functionally, exactly the vessel this research needs — and Graxius StClair, who owns her, is Ujinka’s former student.
Worth knowing: Kaldi Research runs lab ships for hire throughout the Marches. Ujinka could have chartered a professional research vessel. She asked a dead man’s nephew’s crew instead.
Why this matters
Vlen agreed to fund and crew an expedition to Ancient sites, and was shot before he could. Ujinka was then shot dead in her own house, minutes after explaining the research to a second set of potential backers.
Two people, one project, both murdered inside four days. Someone is killing to stop this research — and they knew where and when to find her.
Who would care
Ancients sites cluster in the Spinward Marches, and their technology runs beyond TL25. A reliable method of finding those sites — which is what G-Band Transmissions would be — is worth killing for. Two movements on record already stake their theology on Ancients inheritance:

Church of the Chosen Ones — Vargr are the Ancients’ rightful heirs
Brotherhood of Humaniti — the Ancients broke humanity, and opposing institutions must be destroyed

Nobody has been placed at either murder.
What survives her

The party, who heard it from her directly
Data recovered by Ozy from her house at Dancado — three research notes, transcribed below
Beck’s World, where the fieldwork was, and where Graxius StClair’s ex-wife still is
The University of Regina, her department
The Event Horizon, still the right ship for it, and the decision now nobody’s to accept

The research notes — recovered 196-1105
Three notes Ozy pulled off Ujinka’s computer at Dancado, shared by the GM aboard the Event Horizon on 196-1105. Text as given.
Research Note 1

Subject: Anomalous Attenuation of G-Band Radio Frequencies in Proximity to Purported Precursor Sites.
…While conventional Imperial archaeology treats the Boughene and Regina precursor ruins as chemically inert, localized sensor logs paint a radically different picture. During the 1102 survey, standard subspace telemetry in the G-band suffered a sharp, recursive drop-off. This is not natural solar radiation or iron-ore interference. It mimics a low-frequency, multi-phasic dampening field — a passive ‘footprint’ left by active Monadium structures buried deep beneath the mantle. If my calculations are correct, we can map hidden sites not by looking for ruins, but by looking for the communication ‘dead zones’ they cast across a system.

A later added note states:

Juni and her team will be investigating these G-band signals further at the Beck’s World ancients site. I wonder what secrets she will uncover.

Research Note 2


Log Entry 884-A: Orbiting Gas Giant (Boughene IV). High metal-rich asteroid density.
Telemetry: Ship sensor packet degradation detected at 4.2 GHz (G-band). Automated navigation computers experienced a 0.03-second clock-drift.
Ujinka’s Scribbled Margin Note: “The trader wasn’t lying. The statue he pulled from the asteroid belt is a fragment of a larger anchor array. The signal dampening here perfectly matches the footprint I isolated in the Regina sub-sector. Could something else be hidden away in this system? Vlen Backett thinks the system is worth studying, he has asked to borrow the statue apparently for analysis by one of his contacts.”


Research Note 3

Notes from the Deneb Archeological Conference: The Vilani records from thousands of years ago are fundamentally flawed. They logged the site at Kan as just another ‘precursor society’. They lacked the conceptual leap. They found shimmering glass harder than diamond and containers made of unblemished, un-corroded cobalt, yet they classified it as dead rubbish. It isn’t a collection of disparate alien species. It is a single, unified entity that wielded localised physics like paintbrushes. They didn’t just build structures; they engineered the very matter to resist time.

What the notes establish

The method: Ancient sites cast g-band “dead zones” across a system. Find the dead zone, find the site — no ruins needed. Ujinka attributes the dampening to buried “Monadium structures” (her term; not otherwise explained)
Two confirmed footprints: the Regina sub-sector (the 1102 survey) and Boughene, at the asteroid belt around Boughene IV. Boughene’s official description says there is nothing there of interest
The statue is from Boughene. A trader pulled it from the belt; Ujinka judged it a fragment of a larger anchor array; Vlen borrowed it. It is now the statuette on the Event Horizon. The ship’s scans call it a work of art, not a device, and of Ancients origin
Vlen’s disks corroborate all of this and add a note from Vlen reminding himself to acquire the Professor’s g-band sensor system and use it to scan the Boughene system. Vlen had a target, not just an interest
Juni — Graxius StClair’s ex-wife — has taken the g-band work to the Ancients site on Beck’s World and is there now
Note 3 is a thesis about The Ancients rather than about the signals: one unified entity, not many species, that “wielded localised physics like paintbrushes” and built matter to resist time. The Vilani saw the site at Kan and misfiled it as rubbish

Notes

The crew have not yet decided whether to commit the Event Horizon to continuing the research.
196-1105: the ship left Regina for Alell carrying the notes, the statue and Vlen’s disks. No formal answer given, but the material is aboard

Five large green fields fill the space between the village and the edge of the clearing, two of them on the east side
A river comes in from the west, widens into a pool at the south-west corner, and leaves south through the boundary
A lane leads from the village to a round, bare patch by the pool
A few outbuildings stand alone out near the edges
The whole clearing is ringed by a line of evenly spaced green dots, with jungle beyond

Inferences, not stated: the dots look like a perimeter of posts, lights or defences rather than a wall. The round patch by the pool could be a landing pad. On this map Vaca Goya looks like a farming village, not one of the walled lodge-cities. Confirmed in Session 2026-10-18: the dots are mist-sprayer poles, and it is a farming village. The landing pad is still a guess.
Notes


Session 2026-10-18: visited for Vlen’s homecoming

A small village on a hilltop, “not one of the big ones”. Founded on a nearby uranium deposit; the mines are largely exhausted and it now lives on forestry and farming. Population about a thousand
The green dots on the map are a ring of metal poles topped with motion-sensitive mist sprayers, the village’s sensor grid. Green is good; “if they ever go red, watch out.” That settles the inference above: a sensor grid, not a wall, as smaller settlements use
Shuttles land on the outskirts. Four were already there when the party arrived, more came later
The village hall has terminals. Porter Sajan is magistrate and spiritual leader
Kostas’s old school and old house are here. It looks smaller than he remembers
The GM said the map is AI-generated; the book has none

vargr.title: Vargr
vargr.content:
traveller sota species
Secrets of the Ancients
A species found outside the Imperium, in territory referred to as the Vargr extents. Tusal is believed to have been imported from there roughly a century ago.
Uplifted from Terran canines by The Ancients — which makes them one of the few living things with a direct claim on the Ancients’ legacy, and the Church of the Chosen Ones builds a whole theology on exactly that.
Vargr in the file so far

40th Squadron — organised Vargr power bloc in Gvurrdon, previously bankrolled by the Zhodani
Church of the Chosen Ones — fringe sect holding Vargr to be the Ancients’ rightful heirs
Menorb — agricultural world feeding the Vargr market, raided for it
Rynkatropa — a TL1 sophont species the Vargr enslaved
Tusal — the narcotic that killed Vlen Backett came out of the Vargr extents
Vargr once crossed hundreds of parsecs to consult Vlen himself

On at least one occasion, Vargr travelled hundreds of parsecs to consult Vlen Backett — the single strangest thing in his address book, and the clearest sign his interests reach well beyond Imperial space.
Notes

ven-yasha.title: Ven Yasha
ven-yasha.content:
traveller sota npc rival
Secrets of the Ancients
Rival. A mysterious crime lord, wanted by numerous worlds around Regina. Location unknown.
No-one has ever seen them, so the wanted bulletins are extremely vague. Gender, species, whether “Ven Yasha” is even one person — all unknown.
Connection to Kostas
Kostas Backett has had plenty of issues throughout his career. Just the once, he put out feelers on who was behind one of them, and only one name came back.
Whispers from the shadows, a piece of paper found under a door, hushed exchanges with a contact — whatever went wrong and whenever he went looking for who was behind it, it was just a name and nothing more.
Connection to Vlen
His name kept cropping up in connection with Vlen Backett as well. Iaros Ujinka doesn’t know him personally, only by reputation — and says he is very unpleasant.
So the same name attaches to both Kostas’ career troubles and his murdered uncle’s affairs. That is either the single most important fact in the investigation or a coincidence of a very common bogeyman.
The surviving intruder from the attack at Dancado mentioned Ven Yasha during the crew’s brief questioning before the POC arrived. He gave little else, so the nature of the connection remains unknown.
Odoy’s account — 195-1105
Detective Odoy is investigating Ven Yasha, and told the crew that Yasha killed Vlen Backett and that Vlen was working as a courier for Yasha. He also says the Imperial force that arrived aboard the Alahir is on Regina hunting Yasha, with the Zhodani-spy story serving as cover for their takeover of the inquiry.
None of this is independently verified — it is Odoy’s word, and his own agency and motives are unknown. But it is now the second independent source naming Yasha: the surviving Dancado attacker did so too, before the Imperials removed him from POC custody.
If Odoy is right, the courier theory would explain Vlen’s constant travel and his improbable address book.
Open questions

Who is Ven Yasha?
If Vlen was his courier, what was Vlen carrying — and does it connect to Ujinka’s Research?
Why an Imperial force would cross to Regina to hunt him
How many of Kostas’ career problems are actually theirs? Only one was ever traced.
What the connection to Vlen actually is — creditor, rival, employer, killer?
Whether “he” is right: Ujinka uses it, but nobody has ever seen the man

From inside Winter Shipping â€” 196-1105
Exceedingly Discreet, the Llellewyoly who keeps Winter Shipping’s real records, spoke about Yasha freely on some points and refused others outright. All unverified:

Yasha hired the whole Winter Shipping operation, Harlen included. The company is his
Yasha ordered Iaros Ujinka’s death. Exceedingly Discreet does not understand why, and says so â€” greater understanding of Ancient technology would only raise the value of Ancient artefacts. It does not question his requests
Vlen Backett was a messenger for Yasha â€” “he must have brought bad news, hence his demise”. This is a second, independent version of Detective Odoy’s courier claim
On what Yasha wants from Ancient technology: nobody understands the secrets of the Ancients, but the potential runs to immortality, taking systems, taking the Imperium, destroying armies. Exceedingly Discreet knows of no specific plan
It will not discuss Yasha himself â€” information about Harlen, the hired thugs and Imperial Intelligence is on offer; Yasha is “very much off the cards”, for its own survival. Going against him is “a very bad idea”

Three sources now attach Yasha to the case â€” the Dancado prisoner, Detective Odoy, and now his own organisation.
Notes

vlen-backett's-murder.title: Vlen Backett's Murder
vlen-backett's-murder.content:
traveller sota clue
Secrets of the Ancients
Vlen Backett was murdered in Credo City. From the coroner’s report:

Cause of death: low-velocity gunshot wound to the heart, delivered at close range
Defensive wounds: none
Blood test: 200 ng/mL of the narcotic Tusal — at that level he would barely have been able to stand, let alone fight back. That’s in the “very strong dose” band: pain receptors dulled, heading toward unconsciousness
Augmentations: none

Drugged first, then shot through the heart from close range, with no attempt to defend himself. That reads as an execution rather than a fight or a robbery gone wrong — inference, not stated in the report.
Low-velocity and close range also suggests a quiet weapon and someone who got near enough to use it — worth knowing whether Vlen let them get that close.
What the investigation has since established

Vlen arrived on Regina from Rhylanor three days before he died
He was staying at the Regina Down TAS Hostel, and their camera caught the Three Men at Vlen’s Room — two faces, and a third who kept off camera but had red hair
He was on Regina to meet Iaros Ujinka, a historian he already knew — a meeting arranged before he arrived, and one he never made
Iaros Ujinka has since been murdered too, at Dancado, minutes after explaining the same research to the party — and the party killed one of the two intruders and captured the other, both men from the hostel footage, tying the attacks to one crew
The meeting was to agree funding and a ship for Ujinka’s Research into Ancient technology sites. The first credible motive: he was about to put money and a hull behind an Ancients expedition
Ven Yasha’s name kept cropping up in connection with Vlen
The third carried The Device, which seems to have caused electrical interference
Darrian Jak, a local dealer, sold a lot of Tusal the night Vlen died. Pallod Norrim now claims the short, red-haired Jak killed Vlen, but the crew have not independently verified that conclusion
His Smashed Comms yielded one last number before becoming unusable: Winter Shipping
Admiral Cassius’s network reports that an Imperial police force has taken over a murder inquiry as a state-security matter, with the victim rumoured to be a Zhodani spy. Whether that inquiry and victim are Vlen’s is unconfirmed

Running state in Investigation Status.
Open questions

Who the three men are, and who sent them
Whether the Tusal was self-administered or given to him
Whether this is what the Regina Public Order Commission means by Irregularities in Vlen Backett’s Affairs, or something separate
What he was doing on Rhylanor, and whether he was followed from there
Whether Pallod’s case against Darrian Jak is genuine, mistaken or a cover story
Why Vlen’s last recovered call was to Winter Shipping

Notes

vlen-backett's-true-age.title: Vlen Backett's True Age
vlen-backett's-true-age.content:
traveller sota clue
Secrets of the Ancients
The coroner’s report on Vlen Backett states:

Physiological age: 52
Historical records indicate true age at least 180
No sign of anagathics in his blood system
No augmentations

He was at least 180 years old, had the body of a 52-year-old, and there is no chemical explanation for it.
Every relative who knew him as “every child’s favourite uncle” knew a man who had been doing that for generations. Kostas Backett is 38.
Open questions

How
Whether he knew what he was
Whether it connects to his archaeology, his unnamed contacts among scientists and high nobility, or the Vargr who crossed hundreds of parsecs to consult him
Whether whoever killed him knew

Notes

Kostas researched Vlen’s age again before the meeting with Odoy but found nothing new.
Session 2026-10-18: independent support from the family. Nairal Backett, 92, Kostas’s great-uncle: “I always remember being introduced to him. He was my great-uncle. Never understood it.” And he “didn’t look a day over 50”. If Vlen was great-uncle to a man now 92, he was two generations older than Nairal, which fits the records’ “at least 180” (arithmetic here, not at the table)

vlen-backett.title: Vlen Backett
vlen-backett.content:
traveller sota npc ally
Secrets of the Ancients
Ally. Murdered. “Uncle Vlen” — Kostas Backett’s extended family. Homeworld Alell.
Human. Physiologically 52 at death; historical records put his true age at at least 180, with no anagathics in his blood — see Vlen Backett’s True Age. Killed by a close-range gunshot to the heart while drugged senseless — see Vlen Backett’s Murder.
Took Kostas under his wing plenty of times throughout his troubled career — without Vlen’s “loans” he may never have made it. The scare quotes are the character sheet’s own; on what terms is unstated.
Character
Only at home when travelling. He’d visit Alell for a few weeks or a month or two, delighting friends and family with tales of distant planets and exotic cultures, then the wanderlust would take him off again. A charming old rogue — the more staid relatives disapproved of his questionable, unreliable ways, but he was every child’s favourite uncle.
What he actually does
No-one was ever sure, or whether he was just a drifter amid the stars.

Worked tramp traders, signed on as a deckhand on freighters
Dabbled in archaeology and journalism
Never liked to talk about it, but had quite a collection of firearms and could handle himself in a fight

His strange friends
Mostly other space voyagers — but he received irregular communications from scientists, naval officers, corporate oligarchs, even high nobility. On at least one occasion, Vargr from outside the Imperium travelled hundreds of parsecs to consult with him.
That detail reads differently now: the Vargr were uplifted by The Ancients, Vlen was funding a hunt for Ancients sites, and he was killed with a narcotic that came out of the Vargr extents.
None of these contacts are named. The archaeology plus the reach of that address book is a lot of smoke for a man with no visible job — worth pulling on.
What he was doing on Regina
He came to meet Iaros Ujinka and agree terms on Ujinka’s Research — he was going to provide the funding and a ship for an expedition to sites of Ancient technology. He was killed three days after arriving, before the meeting happened.
Ven Yasha’s name kept cropping up in connection with him.
The last recoverable call from his smashed comms was to Winter Shipping, a logistics and cargo-buying company operating in Credo City and Star Town.
Death
Murdered in Credo City on Regina, late of Regina/Alell. The coroner’s report gives the details (Vlen Backett’s Murder, Vlen Backett’s True Age); the Commission’s letter, below, never mentions that he was killed at all. Notified to Kostas Backett by Pallod Norrim of the Regina Public Order Commission — Handout 2, “Message from Regina”, sealed 190 Standard, 1105 Third Imperium.

Before his death, Vlen left instructions on file with the Public Order Commission naming Kostas as next of kin — to resolve his outstanding affairs on Regina, take possession of his belongings, and transport his remains back to Alell.
A sum of money is deposited with the First Ducal Bank to cover expenses.
His body is in a cryogenic facility in Credo City, to be transferred to Kostas as soon as possible. A TL14+ autodoc can reanimate a corpse kept in a low berth or cryoberth for up to 1D days after death — Vlen died on or before 190-1105 and it is now 193. Probably outside the window, and no one has raised it, but the body is in cryo and Kostas is the legal next of kin who takes possession of it.
The body was transferred to the Event Horizon before the crew left Regina, and is now with them at Alell. When and how the handover happened isn’t recorded.
Kostas is required, in the name of the Duke and under the Public Order Act of 527 (Amended), to travel to Regina with all due haste — or reply so alternate arrangements can be made.
“Given certain irregularities with Vlen Backett’s affairs, it is vitally important that you contact the Public Order Commission upon arrival.” See Irregularities in Vlen Backett’s Affairs.

Two oddities in the letter itself: it’s addressed to the “chattels and corpus of Vlen Backett (deceased)” rather than to Kostas by name, and the Chief Inspector signs off as Pallod Norum having opened as Pallod Norrim.
Pallod now claims that short, red-haired Darrian Jak murdered Vlen and considers the case closed. The crew have not independently verified that conclusion and distrust Pallod’s dismissal of the connected events at Dancado.
The courier theory
On 195-1105 Detective Odoy told the crew that Vlen was a courier for Ven Yasha, and that Yasha killed him — not Jak. Odoy also says the rumour of a murdered Zhodani spy refers to Vlen, that Vlen was not a spy, and that the story is a cover for the Imperial takeover of the inquiry.
All unverified. It would, though, account for a man with no visible job, constant travel, and an address book running from scientists to high nobility — and it sits alongside his last recovered call going to Winter Shipping, where Odoy places the fixer Harlen.
Unresolved: whether courier work and the funding of Ujinka’s Research are the same thread or two separate lives.
Corroboration from inside Winter Shipping â€” 196-1105
Exceedingly Discreet independently described Vlen as a messenger for Ven Yasha â€” “he must have brought bad news, hence his demise”. That is a second source for the courier theory above, and the first to give a motive for the killing, however offhand.
It also says Harlen holds Vlen’s Statuette and Data Crystals â€” property of Vlen’s that never reached the POC-held estate.
Family and money on Alell — Tel’s pre-session handout
What Kostas’s parents told him, second-hand:

His closest living kin on Alell are the Backett Family of Vaca Goya. Tomas Backett never liked him and is probably coming to see “the old charlatan” properly buried
Hans Backett often talked about Vlen having a fortune hidden in his old lodge, and Kostas’s parents are pretty sure Hans is looking for an angle. See Vlen’s Hidden Fortune
About ten years ago Vlen borrowed money from Yusul Parad, head of the Parad Family, a local criminal gang. Kostas’s parents are “pretty sure”, not certain

The family expect a burial, and the crew have the body: it was transferred to the Event Horizon on Regina and is with them at Alell.
Notes


Session 2026-10-18: homecoming in Vaca Goya, burial and will reading tomorrow. Nobody there seemed sad

No will. Porter Sajan had been told Vlen would have a copy on him. It wasn’t among the effects collected on Regina. See Claims on Vlen’s Estate
Brotherhood initiate. Per Aail of the Brotherhood of Humaniti, Vlen was “the initiate Zu”, a member some years ago. He fled their monastery in the dead of night and never returned, having signed over all worldly goods on joining. They now want a “DNA” ceremony for him
A wife? Orisa Backett claims to be his widow and has a wedding certificate. Nobody in the family knew of her
Debts: Yusul Parad says Vlen owes him Cr1,000,000. Marisa Jocell says he owes her his spaceship
Artefacts. Yusul: “I know what your uncle was up to. I know who he was involved with. He was trading in ancient artefacts.” Unverified, but it fits the statuette and Ujinka’s Research
The lodge. Per Nairal Backett, Vlen had a lodge out in the woods, location unknown to the family, and sometimes brought off-world people back to it. Per Rao, he once chartered her to fly him into the middle of nowhere and collected him a week later: Rao’s Map
Age. Nairal, 92, was introduced to Vlen as a child as his great-uncle. See Vlen Backett’s True Age
The cryotube glitched the starport’s customs scanner before passing on a second run. Unexplained

vlen's-hidden-fortune.title: Vlen's Hidden Fortune
vlen's-hidden-fortune.content:
traveller sota clue alell
Secrets of the Ancients
Hans Backett often talked about Vlen Backett having a fortune hidden in his old lodge on Alell. Kostas’s parents are pretty sure Hans is looking for an angle.
Unverified family talk. Nothing says where the lodge is, or whether there’s anything in it.
Worth holding next to the other money questions around Vlen: his “loans” to Kostas, his offer to fund a ship and an expedition for Ujinka’s Research, the Irregularities in Vlen Backett’s Affairs, and the debt to Yusul Parad. A man with no visible job had money from somewhere (connection drawn here, not at the table).
Source: Tel’s pre-session handout on Alell, mostly what Kostas’s parents have told him.
Notes


Session 2026-10-18: the lodge is real, per Nairal Backett: Vlen had “a lodge out in the woods” (not a hunting lodge; those aren’t allowed now), and sometimes came back with off-world people who’d go to the lodge. The family don’t know where it is.

Rao once flew Vlen into the middle of nowhere and collected him a week later. She marked the drop-off on Rao’s Map, which Kostas now has and has shown no one. Kostas thinks that’s the lodge
Yusul Parad says Vlen traded in ancient artefacts, and would take artefacts against the debt. If the fortune is artefacts, a lot of people at this funeral want it (inference)

vlen's-statuette-and-data-crystals.title: Vlen's Statuette and Data Crystals
vlen's-statuette-and-data-crystals.content:
traveller sota item
Secrets of the Ancients
Recovered on 196-1105. A statuette and a set of data disks, taken off Harlen’s desk aboard the hidden base by Ozy in the last thirty seconds before it self-destructed. Harlen was sitting right there with his eyes closed and was not interfered with.
Originally volunteered by Exceedingly Discreet in the small hours of 196-1105, unprompted — “it would be amiss if I didn’t mention that, seeing as you are his nephew” — as possessions of Vlen Backett’s that Harlen was holding.
Are they Vlen’s?
Presumed so, on strong circumstantial grounds, but never confirmed in the fiction. What lines up:

Exceedingly Discreet named a statuette and data crystals in Harlen’s hands, and a statuette and data disks are exactly what was on his desk
They were not part of the estate the POC are holding
Nobody at the table heard Harlen or anyone else say whose they were

The wording also drifted — “crystals” from Exceedingly Discreet, “disks” as described on the desk. Probably the same objects.
The statuette
Ozy recognised it as the same sort of thing that was in Professor Ujinka’s house — his Recon roll was poor and he has no relevant expertise, so this is a layman’s resemblance and no more. If it holds, it makes this the first physical object tying Vlen, Ujinka’s Research and Ven Yasha’s organisation together, and very likely an Ancient artefact.
Vlen was funding Ujinka’s work. Ven Yasha had Ujinka killed for reasons his own records-keeper could not explain. This object sat on the desk of the man who ran Yasha’s company.
Examined — 196-1105
Aboard the Event Horizon, scanned with the ship’s sensors and read against Ujinka’s research notes:
The statuette is a winged pillar of an ivory-like substance. The scans say a work of art, not a technological device, and all evidence points to it being of Ancients origin. It is the statue from Ujinka’s Research Note 2 — pulled by a trader from the asteroid belt around Boughene IV in the Boughene system, which Ujinka judged to be a fragment of a larger anchor array. Her margin note records that Vlen asked to borrow it “for analysis by one of his contacts”. He evidently got it; how it ended up on Harlen’s desk is not explained.
The disks corroborate the match, cover the Boughene asteroid belt and the g-band fluctuations there, and include a note from Vlen reminding himself to acquire the Professor’s g-band sensor system and use it to scan the Boughene system. Only that much of their contents has been described so far.
The data disks
Partly read — see above. The rest not yet described.
Open questions

What the statuette actually is, and whether it is Ancient — Ancient art, an anchor-array fragment from Boughene
What is on the disks — and whether it overlaps with the material Ozy already recovered from Ujinka
Why they were on Harlen’s desk rather than with Ven Yasha
Who Vlen’s “contact” for the analysis was, and whether that contact was Ven Yasha
Whether reading the disks is safe, given what happened to everyone else who knew what Ujinka was working on

Notes


Session 2026-10-18: the GM reminded the table they still have the statuette. They wondered whether it hides Vlen’s will, and the Admiral wanted to break it open. The GM confirmed it was scanned: nothing inside, not hollow

whanga.title: Whanga
whanga.content:
traveller sota location
Secrets of the Ancients
World on the Event Horizon’s route from Regina to Alell: Forboldn → Whanga → Alell, the second of three jumps. Has a gas giant for skimming fuel. The table found the name funny.
Reached in the second week out of Regina; the Event Horizon skimmed the gas giant and jumped for Alell — one parsec. Nobody went down. Nothing else known.
Notes

whisperhawk.title: Whisperhawk
whisperhawk.content:
traveller sota species
Secrets of the Ancients
An animal. One of the most common sights in the Alell jungle — beautiful avians with prodigious wingspans.
Their wings are both locomotion and feeding organs: whisperhawks feed by digesting the insects caught on the sticky undersides. A flock gliding across the canopy at twilight catches hundreds of thousands of insects; the buzzing of the trapped insects and the susurrus of the wind gives the whisperhawk its name.
They are notoriously stupid and have been known to attack humans and vehicles, as well as flagposts, fences, houses and small trees. If threatened, a whisperhawk attacks by wrapping its wings around a larger foe and trying to smother it.
Notes


Session 2026-10-18: flocks with brilliant plumage circled the party’s shuttle over the jungle on the way to Vaca Goya

winter-shipping-station.title: Winter Shipping Station
winter-shipping-station.content:
traveller sota location
Secrets of the Ancients
Destroyed on 196-1105. Harlen triggered its self-destruct while the crew were aboard; the crew escaped by capsule and watched it go.
Called “the station we have in orbit” and “the base” by Exceedingly Discreet, which flew the crew up to it. It was never a station. It was three shipping containers bolted together, hidden inside a container yard at a semi-stable Lagrangian point between Regina and Assiniboia — the same sort of point Assiniboia is noted for. Anything parked there stays put for years.
The approach ran through a constellation of cargo containers, thousands of them, docked into long lines and cubes with some drifting free and untethered, scattered with nav buoys and warning beacons. The launch weaved into the heart of the yard, dipped beneath a trio of old containers, and a concealed hatch opened to dock it inside. Nothing about it was visible or registered as a structure.
This was the destination of the launch runs that took hours longer than a surface-to-Highport trip should — the anomaly Ozy found in the hacked flight manifests.
What was inside

No lights, anywhere. The staff knew their way around in the dark
Doors barely airtight — on a structure in vacuum — and everything cobbled together from salvage
A dock bay of roughly 20 by 50 feet holding the launch and a few sealed crates
An upper level reached by an airlock and ladder, with cover scattered through it, an office, and what looked like a gun emplacement
Harlen’s office, with a statuette and data disks on the desk — see Vlen’s Statuette and Data Crystals
A capsule deck with several escape capsules, each big enough for five. Two were locked and jammed when the smugglers reached them
A crew of smugglers — the GM’s word for them — the number never established. At least seven died

The destruct
Harlen saw Kostas, recognised him, looked at Cassius’ uniform, said “This is suboptimal” and closed his eyes. Every screen in the base went black, an alarm sounded, and a synthesised voice announced destruct sequence activated, detonation imminent, all hands to re-entry capsules, with floor arrows lighting a route to the capsule airlock.
Thirty seconds. No console, no keypad, no spoken command — see Harlen.
About twenty seconds after the capsule launched the base imploded, scrunched up and then blew outward. The capsule rode the edge of the wave down to Regina and landed in wild land outside the Twin Cities, at what looked like a designated recovery point with grav bikes waiting.
What went with it

Whatever Winter Shipping was actually moving through the overlong runs — never established
Any records held on the base rather than in Exceedingly Discreet’s head in Credo
Most of its staff
Possibly Harlen himself, who was last seen at his desk as the count ran down

Notes

winter-shipping.title: Winter Shipping
winter-shipping.content:
traveller sota faction
Secrets of the Ancients
A logistics and cargo-buying company operating in both Credo City and Star Town, the thin strip between Credo and Atora.
The last number called from Vlen Backett’s smashed comms belongs to Winter Shipping. Ozy recovered the number immediately before the damaged device became unusable.
Its advertising targets ship crews struggling with mortgage payments, salaries or repair bills. It offers to buy their cargo with the promise: “Prompt service. No questions asked.”

The premises — reconnoitred 195-1105
Two buildings, one either side of the fence between Credo City and Star Town. The crew approached from the Credo side.

The Credo-side building is closed, with a notice directing callers to the Star Town offices
A huge brute of a man was seen entering the Credo side and emerging on the Star Town side — a crossing that is not supposed to be possible. The crew infer an internal passage through the fence; unconfirmed
The Star Town office interior is very fancy, far smarter than its surroundings. Marid works reception
StClair and Kostas Backett judged the security system unsophisticated — the crew believe they could shut down the alarms

Systems and the launch

Ozy hacked the company’s systems remotely and found almost nothing of interest — suspiciously little. The crew infer a second, unconnected system holding the real records; unconfirmed
The Star Town side operates a launch running up to Regina Highport
Flight records show some of those runs take hours longer than the trip should. Unexplained

Dealings with the crew
On 195-1105 the crew sold their Yori cargo — 3 tons of crystals and gems, bought for Cr54,000 — to Winter Shipping for Cr72,000, using the sale as cover and as a reason to watch the company work. Olso is the contact collecting it.
Connection to Harlen
Detective Odoy says the red-haired man in the case is a fixer called Harlen, connected to Winter Shipping. Odoy’s account is unverified, but it puts the company at the centre of the murder as well as at the end of Vlen’s last call.
Open questions

Why Vlen called the company
Whether the call concerned cargo, money, transport or something else
Who at Winter Shipping spoke to him
What the second system holds, and what the overlong launch runs are doing
What Harlen does here, and whether the company is Ven Yasha’s

Inside the Credo-side building â€” 196-1105
The crew broke in after dark. Kostas disabled the alarms and let the others in through a side access.

The building is mostly dark and empty â€” crate tables, and one lit room in the far corner
That room holds a sealed environmental chamber containing a Llellewyoly, Exceedingly Discreet, working an enormous volume of data on a closed system with no external route in. It calls itself the brains of the operation. This explains the near-empty server Ozy hacked
The passage between the two buildings is real: an unconcealed ramp down into a tunnel running towards the Star Town side. The far end has a ramp up that is closed, with no mechanism visible from the tunnel
Along the tunnel runs a newer pipe with vents at equal intervals â€” purpose unexplained
A storeroom off the tunnel holds empty gin bottles and crates of food not fit for human consumption â€” presumably Exceedingly Discreet’s. StClair ate some and was sick

The company, from the inside â€” 196-1105
All from Exceedingly Discreet, unverified:

Harlen runs Winter Shipping â€” “short-sighted and a poor tactician”, but loyal
Ven Yasha hired them all. The company is Yasha’s
There is a company station in orbit, where Harlen is â€” almost certainly the destination of the overlong launch runs
Exceedingly Discreet controls the launch’s flight path from its console, and has agreed to fly the crew up in exchange for Harlen’s death. Marid is to know nothing about it

Notes

The crew intend to investigate Winter Shipping before meeting Detective Odoy at The Flotsam.
After the Odoy meeting, the crew decided to break in — targets being the unnetworked system, the passage between the buildings, and the launch records.
196-1105: the Credo office revisited — Exceedingly Discreet gone, a receipt for the crew’s own earlier trade the only find. Dead end; the crew left Regina

wochiers.title: Wochiers
wochiers.content:
traveller sota location
Secrets of the Ancients
Atmospheric pressure at sea level is more than four bars, so the population lives in the mountains or in underground complexes.
That high pressure makes Wochiers ideal for certain engineering projects, especially crystal growing.
By tradition, all visitors must bring an offering of a living plant to the hydroponics caves. Suitable plants are available in the starport gift shop.
Notes

yori.title: Yori
yori.content:
traveller sota location
Secrets of the Ancients
Where the party were before this. They left on 185-1105 and arrived at Regina on 193-1105.
They left because of the Regina Public Order Commission’s notice of Vlen Backett’s death — though the GM’s timeline dates that notice five days after the departure. Assumed to be a date slip rather than a mystery.
Notes

yres.title: Yres
yres.content:
traveller sota location
Secrets of the Ancients
The only surface structure is the entrance to the starport — an extremely impressive system of airlocks and tubes reaching from the surface to the seabed. The cities of this balkanised world are all underground and underwater.

Visitors face an additional docking fee of Cr250, an obligatory donation to the Yres Reconstruction and War Widows Fund
The atmosphere is highly radioactive; iodine tablets are available from public dispensers throughout the cities

A reconstruction fund and a war widows fund implies a war worth reconstructing from.
Notes

yusul-parad.title: Yusul Parad
yusul-parad.content:
traveller sota npc alell crime debt
Secrets of the Ancients
Head of the Parad Family, a local criminal gang on Alell with a fearsome reputation.
Ten years ago, Vlen Backett borrowed money from him — Kostas’s parents are pretty sure, not certain. Amount and whether it was repaid unknown. They hope he isn’t at the burial.
Source: Tel’s pre-session handout on Alell, mostly what Kostas’s parents have told him.
Notes


Session 2026-10-18: at the homecoming with his muscle Morgan. “I hate the Backetts, but you, I know I can trust you to do the right thing”, to Kostas

The debt: “just a cool million credits.” He’s restraining himself out of respect for the funeral, but there’ll be trouble if he doesn’t see his money soon
“I know what your uncle was up to. I know who he was involved with. He was trading in ancient artefacts.” If any of those fall into his possession, “we’ll maybe see about getting this debt cleared.” Kostas promised to let him know first
Twice called the Admiral “lippy”, with a hint about accidents
See Claims on Vlen’s Estate

zed-cole.title: Zed Cole
zed-cole.content:
traveller sota npc crew
Secrets of the Ancients
Zed Cole, rolled from the GM’s name tables in Session 2026-10-18. Heard on the recording as “Zed Cole”; spelling per Rich.
He was the friendly one of the Five High Passengers: overly friendly, chatting to everyone, “seeing how things work”. He took the beam laser for one salvo against Delta 2, untrained. Now crew of the Event Horizon, voted in while StClair was away.
As rolled (Core Rulebook p. 92, Quick Characters)

Experienced Combatant: the GM gave him +2 on gun skills, and +1 piloting small craft, not the lab ship. The book’s Experienced Combatant gets Drive/Flyer, Gun Combat, Heavy Weapons, Melee and Recon at around level 2, and characteristic bonuses of +1, +2
Quirk: “has secret allies”. The GM first read “in debt to criminals”, then corrected it after a re-roll. He said the quirk is out-of-game knowledge, and that it’s “interesting” but he has no time to build the subplot yet

Pay
The Admiral floated a six-year unpaid “trial period”, to keep the ship’s cash problems quiet. The table settled on “he gets a salary”. Amount not set.
Notes

zena-antonia.title: Zena Antonia
zena-antonia.content:
traveller sota npc
Secrets of the Ancients
Receptionist at the Regina Down TAS Hostel — where Vlen Backett was staying when he was killed, and where the party are now staying themselves.
She and Kostas Backett have been lightly flirting.
After Kostas was shot at Dancado, he tried to use the injury to win her sympathy. It did not work.
She was not on duty the night Vlen died — that was a different receptionist, since traced and interviewed, who had nothing useful to offer.
The desk sees everyone who comes and goes. She is the closest thing the party have to a source inside the building the murder happened in, and Kostas is the one talking to her.
Notes

zhodani.title: Zhodani
zhodani.content:
traveller sota species
Secrets of the Ancients
A power hostile to, or at least rivalrous with, the Imperium. They have previously propped up the 40th Squadron to threaten the Imperium’s flank.
Nothing else established in play yet.
Notes

Index
Sessions

Session 2026-10-18 — down to Alell and home to Vaca Goya: Rao’s map of where Vlen vanished, no will, and four claimants on the estate, including a widow and a Brotherhood that says he was theirs
Session 2026-10-04 — first space combat: Delta 2 destroyed by missiles, the Event Horizon left at half Hull with a damaged jump drive; passengers delivered to Alell, Cr300,000 collected
Session 2026-09-27 — carthus hunt finished (Kostas down again), Kay explains the growth serum, and a fake Alell patrol ship opens fire on arrival
Session 2026-09-20 — three jumps to Alell: Ozy settles the Helix / Black Horizon row, a passenger turns out to be a blob in a skin suit, and Black Horizon’s carthuses get loose in the shafts
Session 2026-09-13 — passengers and cargo at Regina; Kostas’s surgery; Ujinka’s notes read and the statue traced to Boughene; jump to Forboldn, and a patent row aboard
Session 2026-09-06 — the hidden base boarded and cleared; Harlen blows it by closing his eyes; the statuette and data disks recovered as the crew flee

Session 2026-08-16 — Winter Shipping recced and hacked; Odoy names Ven Yasha as Vlen’s killer and Harlen as the redhead
Session 2026-08-02 — Ujinka lost; Pallod names Jak; Alahir and Winter Shipping leads uncovered

Characters

Kostas Backett — ex-Navy petty officer turned drifter, prosthetic arm, glass eye; unconscious after every fight, patched up again
Ozymandius Forthrast — tinted glasses, long coat, tablet in hand
Tyrus Cassius — retiring Admiral, led the failed mutiny Kostas backed; owns the Implacable

NPCs

Atticus Brown — the Event Horizon’s second gunner; cheap, wanted off-planet
Aylin Boro — retired admiral, hates Cassius, has Kostas mistaken for someone else (contact)
Aail — dancing Brotherhood of Humaniti envoy; claims Vlen signed everything over as Initiate Zu
Orisa Backett — Southern-accented widow nobody knew Vlen had; wedding certificate in hand
Bard Jocell — Marisa’s son; fawns over off-world nobles and tourists
Countess Parasii — ruler of Uakye; no connection to the investigation
Darrian Jak — short red-haired Tusal dealer in POC custody; the crew think he’s a fall guy for being red-haired
Detective Odoy — met the party at the Flotsam; says Ven Yasha killed Vlen and the spy story is a cover
Gunner Gunnerson — the Event Horizon’s one-eyed ex-Marine gunner; carried both firefights aboard the base
Gunter Backett — Tomas’s 15-year-old son; always wants Kostas’s off-world stories
Five High Passengers — the drunk, the recluse, the noble, the friendly one (now crew) and the blob; Cr60,000 each at Alell
Exceedingly Discreet — Llellewyoly that ran Winter Shipping’s records and wanted Harlen dead; vanished from the Credo office 196-1105
Hans Backett — hunter and trapper, Tomas’s brother, Backett co-head; talks up Vlen’s hidden fortune, looking for an angle
Henna Backett — Kostas’s mother; dotes on the Admiral, “so good to see you again”
Harlen — red-haired fixer who ran Winter Shipping for Ven Yasha; blew the base by closing his eyes, fate unknown
Marid — receptionist at Winter Shipping’s Star Town office
Marisa Jocell — insufferable socialite leading the Jocell delegation; says Vlen owes her his spaceship
Merrick Backett — Kostas’s father; “you look a mess, boy”
Morgan — Yusul Parad’s unarmed muscle
Nairal Backett — Kostas’s 92-year-old great-uncle; Vlen was his great-uncle; knows of Vlen’s lodge
Olso — the crew’s Winter Shipping contact; collecting their Yori cargo
Pallod Norrim — Chief Inspector; named Jak as Vlen’s killer, now refuses the crew’s calls
Pedro — Black Horizon security guard; stunned two carthuses, lost a chunk of shoulder
Rao — Alell shuttle pilot; once flew Vlen into the jungle and fetched him a week later
Rok — Helix’s hyena-man rep aboard
Porter Sajan — Vaca Goya’s porter, magistrate and spiritual leader; handed the estate claims to Kostas
Khei — Black Horizon’s cat-woman rep aboard (once noted as Kay); Ozy’s lover; offered the growth serum for the crew’s silence
Juni — StClair’s ex-wife; carrying Ujinka’s g-band work at the Beck’s World Ancients site
Iaros Ujinka — history professor at Dancado, StClair’s mentor; murdered mid-meeting with the party
Talia — the Event Horizon’s steward, Steward 3; “the underpaid”, now Cr4,000; found the skin suit
Tomas Backett — merchant, Backett head in Vaca Goya, Hans’s brother; never liked Vlen; Ozy is his “neutral third party”
Vlen Backett — “Uncle Vlen”, restless family rogue with an improbable address book (ally, murdered)
Ven Yasha — unseen crime lord wanted around Regina; owns Winter Shipping, ordered Ujinka’s death (rival)
Yusul Parad — Parad gang boss; says Vlen owes him Cr1,000,000 and traded in ancient artefacts
Zed Cole — the friendly ex-passenger, now crew; Experienced Combatant with secret allies
Zena Antonia — receptionist at the Regina Down TAS Hostel; flirting with Kostas

Locations

Alell — Backett family homeworld; old First Imperium hunting world, now walled lodge-cities, Law Level 12; no highport
Alell Starport — Class B surface port; First Imperium stepped pyramid by a walled town
Assiniboia — the gas giant Regina orbits; several semi-stable Lagrangian points
Atora — Regina’s other city, traditionalist rival to Credo
Beck’s World — former pirate base; Ujinka’s research site, StClair’s ex-wife is still there
Boughene — closed scout base, “nothing of interest” — and a g-band footprint and Ancient anchor array in its asteroid belt
Corridor — sector where Tusal is grown
Credo City — capital of Regina, 87 million; where Vlen was murdered
Dancado — forested region north of Credo, the Duke’s private property; where Ujinka was killed
Dranxi Jungle — Alell jungle; First Imperium hunting lodges at its heart
Efate — high-TL crossroads, almost as influential as Regina; 213th Fleet HQ
Forboldn — first leg of the route to Alell; refuelled at the gas giant, nobody went down
Feri — civil war underway, provisional Amber classification
Gvurrdon — Vargr region; the 40th Squadron’s ground
Kan — site the Vilani misfiled as a precursor society; named in Ujinka’s conference notes
Knorbes — Imperial game reserve; technologically restricted zone
Menorb — agricultural world feeding the Vargr market, plagued by raiders
Pixie — forward operating base of the 213th Fleet; visitors discouraged
Regina — a moon, seat of the Duchy, largest trade hub in the sector, Law Level 9
Regina Down TAS Hostel — where Vlen stayed and was killed
Regina Highport — Class A port in orbit; one of the largest in the Marches
Rhylanor — where Vlen travelled from, three days before his death
Roup — Kostas’ homeworld; water world of seaweed rafts
Spinward Marches — sector containing the Regina subsector
Startown — the downport strip; violent, corrupt and profitable
The Flotsam — bar; venue for Odoy’s 195-1105 meeting
Uakye — tidally locked; Countess Parasii resents Efate
Vaca Goya — the Backetts’ hilltop farming village, pop. ~1,000, ringed by mist-sprayer poles
Whanga — second hop on the route to Alell; refuelled at the gas giant, nobody went down
Winter Shipping Station — three containers hidden in a Lagrangian container yard, not a station at all; destroyed 196-1105
Wochiers — four-bar atmosphere, crystal growing, bring a plant
Yori — where the party travelled from, leaving 185-1105
Yres — balkanised undersea world, radioactive atmosphere

Ships

Alahir — non-standard Scout Service-registered ship that carried Imperial Intelligence to Regina; has departed
Delta 2 — Far Trader posing as an Alell patrol ship; fired missiles, destroyed by the Event Horizon
Event Horizon — the party’s Lab Ship; in orbit at Alell, Zed Cole now crew, Hull 47 of 124, jump drive damaged, no missiles, one jump of fuel
Implacable — Pinnace carried by the Event Horizon; one fixed beam laser
Ship Finances — the Event Horizon’s ledger: balance, monthly costs, money owed in and out

Factions

213th Fleet — Imperial fleet, HQ at Efate, forward base at Pixie
40th Squadron — organised Vargr power bloc in Gvurrdon, once bankrolled by the Zhodani
Backett Family — Vlen and Kostas’s family, of Vaca Goya on Alell
Black Horizon — secretive research company chartering lab space on the Event Horizon; won the patent row, lost its specimens into the shafts, kept the serum that grew them
Brotherhood of Humaniti — human unity cult; Vlen was a runaway initiate, and they claim his estate
Church of the Chosen Ones — fringe Vargr sect; hold Vargr to be the Ancients’ heirs
First Ducal Bank — holds the money set aside for Kostas’ expenses on Regina
First Imperium — Vilani-era Imperium; Alell was settled as it died
Helix — honest, bureaucratic research company chartering lab space on the Event Horizon; lost the patent row and resents it
Imperium — the Third Imperium, dominant polity; Vlen had contacts beyond its borders
Jocell Family — starport branch of the Backetts; look down on their country cousins
Kaldi Research — private corporation running lab ships for hire across the Marches
Parad Family — Alell criminal gang with a fearsome reputation, unrelated to the Backetts
Regina Public Order Commission — Regina’s civil authority; holding Vlen’s estate; released his body to the crew
Travellers’ Aid Society — TAS; Vlen stayed at their hostel, their camera caught the three men
University of Regina — Ujinka’s Department of History
Winter Shipping — logistics and cargo-buying company; Vlen’s last call, Harlen’s employer, two buildings straddling the fence, owned by Ven Yasha

Laws

Assumption of Custody — the POC can hold suspects a month without trial; Travellers are swept routinely

Events

First Frontier War — its aftermath let the 40th Squadron carve out a kingdom

Species

Rynkatropa — whistling sea-slug sophonts, enslaved by the Vargr at TL1
Cadgeree — Alell savannah winged snake; drops on prey and snaps its spine
Carthus — pale, boneless desert cave-dweller; Black Horizon’s serum-grown specimens, hunted down aboard the Event Horizon
Droyne — kept by the Ancients as pets or servants; organised into oyntrips
Lambdragon — Alell herbivore; a stampede can flatten a tank
Llellewyoly — ‘Dandelions’; plant-like sophonts with dozens of simultaneous titles
Maleficent — jet-black tentacled Alell predator, possibly not native to the world
Whisperhawk — Alell canopy avian; stupid, and smothers what threatens it
The Ancients — precursors, 300,000 years gone; scattered Humaniti, uplifted the Vargr, tech beyond TL25
Vargr — uplifted from Terran canines by the Ancients; some once crossed hundreds of parsecs to see Vlen
Zhodani — rivals of the Imperium; have funded the 40th Squadron against it

Items

Black Horizon’s Growth Serum — grew the carthus embryos instantly; offered to the crew for their silence
Rao’s Map — moth-eaten map marking where Rao dropped Vlen in the jungle; Kostas has it, unshown
Smashed Comms — yielded Winter Shipping as Vlen’s last call before becoming unusable
Tusal — illegal seaweed-derived narcotic; Vlen was full of it when he was shot
Vlen’s Statuette and Data Crystals — Ancient winged pillar from Boughene’s asteroid belt, a fragment of an anchor array; disks hold Vlen’s plan to scan Boughene; scanned, not hollow

Clues

Ancients Extinction Theories — competing accounts of how the Ancients vanished
Claims on Vlen’s Estate — no will, four claimants: the Brotherhood, a widow, Yusul’s million, Marisa’s spaceship
Being Followed — apparent POC grav car at Dancado; local officers deny it was theirs
G-Band Transmissions — g-band dead zones cast by buried Ancient structures; found at Regina and Boughene
Investigation Status — running timeline and open threads
Ujinka’s Research — her three recovered notes: the dead-zone method, the Boughene statue, and the Ancients as one entity

The Device — carried by the third man; seems to have caused electrical interference
Three Men at Vlen’s Room — TAS footage; two faces, one red-haired man who stayed off camera
Vlen Backett’s Murder — drugged, then shot through the heart at close range
Vlen Backett’s True Age — at least 180 years old, body of a 52-year-old, no anagathics; great-uncle to a 92-year-old
Vlen’s Hidden Fortune — Vlen’s lodge in the woods, location unknown; Hans is after it
